bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 起閼逢攝提格，盡屠維協洽，凡六年。

translations.literal: From Efeng Shetige through Tuwei Xiehe; six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Efeng Shetige through Tuwei Xiehe—six years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，三月，詔曰：「蓋聞有功不賞，有罪不誅，雖唐、虞不能化天下。

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the third month, an edict said: "I have heard that if merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, even Tang and Yu could not transform all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the third month, an edict said: "I have heard that if merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, even Tang and Yu could not transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 今膠東相王成，勞來不怠，流民自佔八萬餘口，治有異等之效。

translations.literal: Now Wang Cheng, Chancellor of Jiaodong, toils to comfort the people without slackening; displaced commoners of themselves registered more than eighty thousand mouths, and his governance showed effects of extraordinary grade.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Cheng, Chancellor of Jiaodong, toils to comfort the people without slackening; displaced commoners registered of their own accord more than eighty thousand persons, and his governance showed extraordinary results.

sentences.zh: 其賜成爵關內侯，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: Let Cheng be granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, with emolument of two thousand bushels, middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: Let Cheng be granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, with emolument of two thousand bushels, middle grade.

sentences.zh: 」未及徵用，會病卒官。

translations.literal: " Before he could be summoned to office, he fell ill and died in his post.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he could be summoned to office, he fell ill and died in his post.

sentences.zh: 後詔使丞相、御史問郡、國上計長史、守丞以政令得失。

translations.literal: Later an edict sent the chancellor and the imperial secretary to question the chief clerks, governors, and assistant governors of commanderies and kingdoms who presented annual accounts on the gains and losses of government orders.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict sent the chancellor and the imperial secretary to question the chief clerks, governors, and assistant governors of commanderies and kingdoms presenting annual accounts on the gains and losses of government policy.

sentences.zh: 或對言：「前膠東相成偽自增加以蒙顯賞，是後俗吏多為虛名」-{云}-。

translations.literal: Some answered, saying: "The former Chancellor of Jiaodong Cheng falsely inflated his own figures to win conspicuous reward; after that, vulgar officials often made empty reputations" -{云}-.
translations.idiomatic: Some answered: "The former Chancellor of Jiaodong Cheng falsely inflated his own figures to win conspicuous reward; after that, vulgar officials often made empty reputations" -{云}-.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，四月，戊申，立子奭為皇太子，以丙吉為太傅，太中大夫疏廣為少傅。

translations.literal: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, Prince Shi was established as heir apparent; Bing Ji was made Grand Tutor and Palace Grandee Shuguang Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fourth month, on wushen, Prince Shi was established as heir apparent; Bing Ji was made Grand Tutor and Palace Grandee Shuguang Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 封太子外祖父許廣漢為平恩侯。

translations.literal: The crown prince's maternal grandfather Xu Guanghan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ping'en.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's maternal grandfather Xu Guanghan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Ping'en.

sentences.zh: 又封霍光兄孫中郎將雲為冠陽侯。

translations.literal: Huo Guang's brother's grandson, Palace Cadet Yun, was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huo Guang's brother's grandson, Palace Cadet Yun, was also enfeoffed as Marquis of Guanyang.

sentences.zh: 霍顯聞立太子，怒恚不食，歐血，曰：「此乃民間時子，安得立！

translations.literal: Huo Xian heard that the heir was established, grew furious, refused food, and spat blood, saying: "This is a commoner's child of the streets—how can he be established!
translations.idiomatic: Huo Xian heard the heir was established, grew furious, refused food, and spat blood, saying, "This is a commoner's child of the streets—how can he be established!"

sentences.zh: 即-{后}-有子，反為王邪！

translations.literal: If the -{后}- had a son, would he not instead be made king!
translations.idiomatic: If the -{后}- had a son, would he not instead be made king!

sentences.zh: 」復教皇后令毒太子。

translations.literal: " She again instructed the empress to have the heir poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " She again instructed the empress to have the heir poisoned.

sentences.zh: 皇后數召太子賜食，保、阿輒先嘗之，-{后}-挾毒不得行。

translations.literal: The empress repeatedly summoned the heir and bestowed food; his nurses and tutors always tasted it first, and the -{后}-'s plot to use poison could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The empress repeatedly summoned the heir and bestowed food; his nurses and tutors always tasted it first, and the -{后}-'s plot to use poison could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: ----3五月，甲申，丞相賢以老病乞骸骨；

translations.literal: ----3 In the fifth month, on jiashen, Chancellor Xian, owing to age and illness, begged to surrender his bones;
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the fifth month, on jiashen, Chancellor Xian, owing to age and illness, begged to surrender his bones;

sentences.zh: 賜黃金百斤、安車、駟馬，罷就第。

translations.literal: he was granted a hundred jin of gold, a comfort carriage, and a four-horse team, and dismissed to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: he was granted a hundred jin of gold, a comfort carriage, and a four-horse team, and dismissed to his residence.

sentences.zh: 丞相致仕自賢始。

translations.literal: A chancellor's retirement from office began with Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Retirement of a chancellor from office began with Xian.

sentences.zh: ----4六月，壬辰，以魏相為丞相。

translations.literal: ----4 In the sixth month, on renchen, Wei Xiang was made chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: ----4 In the sixth month, on renchen, Wei Xiang was made chancellor.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，丙吉為御史大夫，疏廣為太子太傅，廣兄子受為少傅。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Bing Ji became Imperial Secretary, Shuguang became Grand Tutor of the Heir, and Shuguang's elder brother's son Shou became Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Bing Ji became Imperial Secretary, Shuguang became Grand Tutor of the Heir, and Shuguang's elder brother's son Shou became Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 太子外祖父平恩侯許伯，以為太子少，白使其弟中郎將舜監護太子家。

translations.literal: The heir's maternal grandfather, the Marquis of Ping'en, Lord Xu, thinking the heir young, reported and had his younger brother, Palace Cadet Shun, oversee and guard the heir's household.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's maternal grandfather, Marquis of Ping'en Lord Xu, thinking the heir young, reported and had his younger brother, Palace Cadet Shun, oversee the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 上以問廣，廣對曰：「太子，國儲副君，師友必於天下英俊，不宜獨親外家許氏。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Shuguang; Shuguang answered: "The heir is the state's stored successor and deputy lord; teachers and friends must be chosen from the outstanding men of all under Heaven—it is not fitting to favor only the maternal kin, the Xu clan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Shuguang; Shuguang answered: "The heir is the state's stored successor and deputy lord; teachers and friends must be chosen from outstanding men across the realm—it is not fitting to favor only the maternal Xu clan."

sentences.zh: 且太子自有太傅、少傅，官屬已備，今復使舜護太子家，示陋，非所以廣太子德於天下也。

translations.literal: Moreover the heir already has Grand Tutor and Junior Tutor; his official staff is complete. Now to send Shun again to guard the heir's household shows narrowness and is not the way to spread the heir's virtue through all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the heir already has Grand and Junior Tutors; his staff is complete. To send Shun again to guard the heir's household shows narrowness and is not how to spread the heir's virtue through the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上善其言，以語魏相，相免冠謝曰：「此非臣等所能及。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and told Wei Xiang; Xiang removed his cap and apologized, saying: "This is not what your servants could reach.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words and told Wei Xiang; Xiang removed his cap and apologized: "This is not what we could reach."

sentences.zh: 」廣由是見器重。

translations.literal: " Shuguang from this was seen as heavily valued.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuguang from this was held in high regard.

sentences.zh: ----5京師大雨雹，大行丞東海蕭望之上疏，言大臣任政，一姓專權之所致。

translations.literal: ----5 In the capital region great hail fell; Assistant Director of the Major Line Xiao Wangzhi of Donghai submitted a memorial saying that great ministers holding government and one clan monopolizing power had caused it.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In the capital region great hail fell; Assistant Director of the Major Line Xiao Wangzhi of Donghai submitted a memorial saying great ministers holding government and one clan monopolizing power had caused it.

sentences.zh: 上素聞望之名，拜為謁者。

translations.literal: The emperor had long heard Wangzhi's name and appointed him Usher.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long heard Wangzhi's name and appointed him Usher.

sentences.zh: 時上博延賢俊，民多上書言便宜，輒下望之問狀；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor broadly sought worthy and outstanding men; the people often submitted memorials on expedient measures, and he would send them down to Wangzhi to examine the facts;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor broadly sought worthy men; the people often submitted memorials on expedient measures, and he would send them down to Wangzhi to examine the facts;

sentences.zh: 高者請丞相、御史，次者中二千石試事，滿歲以狀聞；

translations.literal: the highest were referred to chancellor and imperial secretary, the next given trial office at two thousand bushels, middle grade, and after a full year reported on their performance;
translations.idiomatic: the highest were referred to chancellor and imperial secretary, the next given trial office at two thousand bushels, middle grade, and after a full year reported on their performance;

sentences.zh: 下者報聞，罷。

translations.literal: the lowest were reported as heard and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: the lowest were reported as heard and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 所白處奏皆可。

translations.literal: Wherever he reported and memorialized, all was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he reported and memorialized, all was approved.

sentences.zh: ----6冬，十月，詔曰：「乃者九月壬申地震，朕甚懼焉。

translations.literal: ----6 In winter, the tenth month, an edict said: "Recently on renshen in the ninth month there was an earthquake; We are greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In winter, the tenth month, an edict said: "Recently on renshen in the ninth month there was an earthquake; We are greatly afraid."

sentences.zh: 有能箴朕過失，及賢良方正直言極諫之士，以匡朕之不逮，毋諱有司。

translations.literal: Those who can admonish Our faults, and worthy and upright men who speak plainly and remonstrate to the utmost, to correct Our shortcomings—let them not fear the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Those who can admonish Our faults, and worthy and upright men who speak plainly and remonstrate to the utmost, to correct Our shortcomings—let them not fear the responsible offices."

sentences.zh: 朕既不德，不能附遠，是以邊境屯戍未息。

translations.literal: We lack virtue and cannot draw the distant near; therefore border garrisons and frontier defense have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: We lack virtue and cannot draw the distant near; therefore border garrisons and frontier defense have not ceased."

sentences.zh: 今復飭兵重屯，久勞百姓，非所以綏天下也。

translations.literal: Now again to order troops and mass garrisons long wearies the hundred clans—it is not the way to pacify all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Now again to order troops and mass garrisons long wearies the people—it is not how to pacify the realm."

sentences.zh: 其罷車騎將軍、右將軍屯兵。

translations.literal: Let the garrison troops of the General of Chariots and Cavalry and the Right General be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Let the garrison troops of the General of Chariots and Cavalry and the Right General be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「池籞未御幸者，假與貧民。

translations.literal: " Another edict said: "Ponds and parks not yet visited by Us—lend them to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: " Another edict said: "Ponds and parks not yet visited by Us—lend them to the poor."

sentences.zh: 郡國宮館勿復修治。

translations.literal: Let commanderies and kingdoms not again repair palace lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Let commanderies and kingdoms not again repair palace lodges."

sentences.zh: 流民還歸者，假公田，貸種食，且勿算事。

translations.literal: Displaced people who return home—lend them public fields, loan seed and food, and for the time being do not assess their labor obligations.
translations.idiomatic: Displaced people who return home—lend them public fields, loan seed and food, and for the time being do not assess their labor obligations."

sentences.zh: 」----7霍氏驕侈縱橫。

translations.literal: " ----7 The Huo clan was arrogant, extravagant, and ran rampant.
translations.idiomatic: " ----7 The Huo clan was arrogant, extravagant, and ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 太夫人顯，廣治第室，作乘輿輦，加畫，繡絪馮，黃金塗；

translations.literal: The Grand Lady Xian extensively built mansion chambers, made imperial carriages and palanquins, added painted decoration, embroidered cushions and canopies, and gilding;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Lady Xian extensively built mansions, made imperial carriages and palanquins, added painted decoration, embroidered cushions and canopies, and gilding;

sentences.zh: 韋絮薦輪，侍婢以五采絲輓顯遊戲第中；

translations.literal: with rush padding and felt mats on the wheels; serving maids used five-colored silk to draw Xian roaming and sporting within the mansion;
translations.idiomatic: with rush padding and felt mats on the wheels; serving maids used five-colored silk to draw Xian roaming within the mansion;

sentences.zh: 與監奴馮子都亂。

translations.literal: she had illicit relations with the overseer slave Feng Zidu.
translations.idiomatic: she had illicit relations with the overseer slave Feng Zidu.

sentences.zh: 而禹、山亦並繕治第宅，走馬馳逐平樂館。

translations.literal: Yu and Shan also together repaired mansions and galloped horses racing through the Pingle lodges.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Shan also repaired mansions and galloped horses racing through the Pingle lodges.

sentences.zh: 雲當朝請，數稱病私出，多從賓客，張圍獵黃山苑中，使倉頭奴上朝謁，莫敢譴者。

translations.literal: Yun should have attended court audiences but repeatedly claimed illness and went out privately with many retainers, spreading nets to hunt in Huangshan Park, sending a granary-head slave to attend court audience in his place—none dared reprove him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun should have attended court but repeatedly claimed illness and went out privately with many retainers, spreading nets to hunt in Huangshan Park, sending a granary-head slave to attend court in his place—none dared reprove him.

sentences.zh: 顯及諸女晝夜出入長信宮殿中，亡期度。

translations.literal: Xian and the various daughters went in and out of the Changxin Palace day and night without schedule or measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xian and the various daughters went in and out of Changxin Palace day and night without schedule or measure.

sentences.zh: 帝自在民間，聞知霍氏尊盛日久，內不能善。

translations.literal: The emperor, from when he was among the common people, had heard of the Huo clan's long-standing eminence and inwardly could not approve.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, from when he lived among the common people, had heard of the Huo clan's long eminence and inwardly could not approve.

sentences.zh: 既躬親朝政，御史大夫魏相給事中。

translations.literal: Once he personally took charge of court affairs, Imperial Secretary Wei Xiang served within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once he personally took charge of court affairs, Imperial Secretary Wei Xiang served within the palace.

sentences.zh: 顯謂禹、雲、山：「女曹不務奉大將軍餘業，今大夫給事中，他人壹間女，能復自救邪！

translations.literal: Xian said to Yu, Yun, and Shan: "You do not strive to uphold the Grand General's legacy; now the Grand Secretary serves within the palace—if others drive in one wedge, can you still save yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Xian said to Yu, Yun, and Shan: "You do not strive to uphold the Grand General's legacy; now the Grand Secretary serves within the palace—if others drive in one wedge, can you still save yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 」後兩家奴爭道，霍氏奴入御史府，欲躢大夫門；

translations.literal: " Later two households' slaves disputed the road; a Huo slave entered the Imperial Secretary's office and wished to trample the Grand Secretary's gate;
translations.idiomatic: " Later two households' slaves disputed the road; a Huo slave entered the Imperial Secretary's office and wished to trample the Grand Secretary's gate;

sentences.zh: 御史為叩頭謝，乃去。

translations.literal: the Imperial Secretary knocked his head in apology for them, and they then left.
translations.idiomatic: the Imperial Secretary knocked his head in apology for them, and they then left.

sentences.zh: 人以謂霍氏，顯等始知憂。

translations.literal: People told the Huo clan, and Xian and the others first knew to worry.
translations.idiomatic: People told the Huo clan, and Xian and the others first knew to worry.

sentences.zh: 會魏大夫為丞相，數燕見言事；

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Wei became chancellor, he was repeatedly granted private audiences to speak on affairs;
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretary Wei became chancellor, he was repeatedly granted private audiences to speak on affairs;

sentences.zh: 平恩侯與侍中金安上等徑出入省中。

translations.literal: the Marquis of Ping'en and Palace Attendant Jin Anshang and others went directly in and out of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis of Ping'en and Palace Attendant Jin Anshang and others went directly in and out of the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 時霍山領尚書，上令吏民得奏封事，不關尚書，群臣進見獨往來，於是霍氏甚惡之。

translations.literal: At that time Huo Shan headed the Imperial Secretariat; the emperor allowed officials and commoners to submit sealed memorials without routing through the Secretariat, and ministers entering audience came and went alone—thereupon the Huo clan greatly hated this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Huo Shan headed the Imperial Secretariat; the emperor allowed officials and commoners to submit sealed memorials without routing through the Secretariat, and ministers entering audience came and went alone—the Huo clan greatly hated this.

sentences.zh: 上頗聞霍氏毒殺-{許后}-而未察，乃徙光女婿度遼將軍、未央衛尉、平陵侯范明友為光祿勳，出次婿諸吏、中郎將、羽林監任勝為安定太守。

translations.literal: The emperor had somewhat heard that the Huo clan poisoned -{許后}- but had not investigated; he then transferred Guang's son-in-law, General Who Crosses the Liao, Commandant of Weiyang, Marquis of Pingling Fan Mingyou to Palace Grandee, and sent out his second son-in-law, Gentleman-of-the-Various-Offices, Palace Cadet, Colonel of the Forest of Feathers Ren Sheng as Governor of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had somewhat heard the Huo clan poisoned -{許后}- but had not investigated; he transferred Guang's son-in-law, General Who Crosses the Liao, Commandant of Weiyang, Marquis of Pingling Fan Mingyou to Palace Grandee, and sent out his second son-in-law, Gentleman-of-the-Various-Offices, Palace Cadet, Colonel of the Forest of Feathers Ren Sheng as Governor of Anding.

sentences.zh: 數月，復出光姊婿給事中、光祿大夫張朔為蜀郡太守，群孫婿中郎將王漢為武威太守。

translations.literal: Within several months he again sent out Guang's elder sister's son-in-law, Attendant Within the Palace, Palace Grandee Zhang Shuo as Governor of Shu commandery, and the clan grandson's son-in-law, Palace Cadet Wang Han as Governor of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Within several months he again sent out Guang's elder sister's son-in-law, Attendant Within the Palace, Palace Grandee Zhang Shuo as Governor of Shu, and the clan grandson's son-in-law, Palace Cadet Wang Han as Governor of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復徙光長女婿長樂衛尉鄧廣漢為少府。

translations.literal: Shortly after, he again transferred Guang's eldest son-in-law, Commandant of Changle Wei, Deng Guanghan to Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, he again transferred Guang's eldest son-in-law, Commandant of Changle Wei, Deng Guanghan to Director of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，更以張安世為衛將軍，兩宮衛尉、城門、北軍兵屬焉。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Zhang Anshi was again made General of the Guard; the commandants of the two palaces, the gate guards, and the Northern Army all were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Zhang Anshi was again made General of the Guard; the commandants of the two palaces, the gate guards, and the Northern Army were all placed under him.

sentences.zh: 以霍禹為大司馬，冠小冠，亡印綬；

translations.literal: Huo Yu was made Grand Marshal, wearing the small cap, without seal and ribbon;
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yu was made Grand Marshal, wearing the small cap, without seal and ribbon;

sentences.zh: 罷其屯兵官屬，特使禹官名與光俱大司馬者。

translations.literal: his garrison troops and official staff were dismissed, and Yu alone was specially left with the same office title as Guang had held, Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: his garrison troops and official staff were dismissed, and Yu alone was specially left with the same office title Guang had held, Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 又收范明友度遼將軍印綬，但為光祿勳；

translations.literal: Fan Mingyou's seal and ribbon as General Who Crosses the Liao were again taken back; he served only as Palace Grandee;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Mingyou's seal and ribbon as General Who Crosses the Liao were taken back; he served only as Palace Grandee;

sentences.zh: 及光中女婿趙平為散騎、騎都尉、光祿大夫，將屯兵，又收平騎都尉印綬。

translations.literal: and Guang's middle son-in-law Zhao Ping, Colonel of Loose Riders, Commandant of Cavalry, Palace Grandee, who commanded garrison troops, again had his Commandant of Cavalry seal and ribbon taken back.
translations.idiomatic: and Guang's middle son-in-law Zhao Ping, Colonel of Loose Riders, Commandant of Cavalry, Palace Grandee, who commanded garrison troops, again had his Commandant of Cavalry seal and ribbon taken back.

sentences.zh: 諸領胡、越騎、羽林及兩宮衛將屯兵，悉易以所親信許、史子弟代之。

translations.literal: All who headed the Hu and Yue cavalry, the Forest of Feathers, and the guard generals' garrison troops of the two palaces were entirely replaced with trusted Xu and Shi clan younger kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: All who headed the Hu and Yue cavalry, the Forest of Feathers, and the guard generals' garrison troops of the two palaces were replaced with trusted Xu and Shi clan younger kinsmen.

sentences.zh: ----8初，孝武之世，徵發煩數，百姓貧耗，窮民犯法，奸軌不勝，於是使張湯、趙禹之屬，條定法令，作見知故縱、監臨部主之法，緩深、故之罪，急縱、出之誅。

translations.literal: ----8 In the beginning, in the age of Emperor Wu of Filial Piety, levies and summons were frequent and troublesome; the hundred clans grew poor and depleted; the destitute violated the law and wicked paths could not be mastered. Thereupon Zhang Tang, Zhao Yu, and their sort were sent to itemize and fix laws and statutes, making the laws on witnessing knowledge yet conniving release and on supervising and arriving as department heads—relaxing penalties for deep and old offenses, hastening punishments for conniving release.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 In the beginning, in the age of Emperor Wu, levies and summons were frequent; the people grew poor; the destitute violated the law and wicked paths could not be mastered. Zhang Tang, Zhao Yu, and their sort were sent to itemize laws and statutes, making laws on witnessing knowledge yet conniving release and on supervising and arriving as department heads—relaxing penalties for deep and old offenses, hastening punishments for conniving release.

sentences.zh: 其後奸猾巧法轉相比況，禁罔浸密，律令煩苛，文書盈於-{几}-閣，典者不能遍睹。

translations.literal: Afterward the crafty and slippery twisted the law in mutual comparison; prohibitions and nets grew ever denser, statutes and ordinances vexatious and harsh, documents overflowing the -{几}- cabinets so that those in charge could not view them all.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the crafty twisted the law in mutual comparison; prohibitions grew ever denser, statutes vexatious and harsh, documents overflowing the -{几}- cabinets so those in charge could not view them all.

sentences.zh: 是以郡國承用者駁，或罪同而論異，奸吏因緣為市，所欲活則傅生議，所欲陷則予死比，議者咸冤傷之。

translations.literal: Therefore what commanderies and kingdoms applied was inconsistent; sometimes the crime was the same but the judgment differed. Wicked officials used the opportunity as a market—whom they wished to spare they clothed with living arguments; whom they wished to trap they gave death analogies. All who discussed it alike grieved at the injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore what commanderies and kingdoms applied was inconsistent; sometimes the crime was the same but the judgment differed. Wicked officials used the opportunity as a market—whom they wished to spare they clothed with living arguments; whom they wished to trap they gave death analogies. sentences.zh: 廷尉史鉅鹿路溫舒上書曰：「臣聞齊有無知之禍而桓公以興，晉有驪姬之難而文公用伯。

translations.literal: Clerk of the Commandant of Justice Lu Wenshu of Julu submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that Qi had the calamity of Wuzhi yet Duke Huan thereby rose; Jin had the trouble of Lady Li yet Duke Wen thereby used hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk of the Commandant of Justice Lu Wenshu of Julu submitted a memorial: "Your servant has heard that Qi had the calamity of Wuzhi yet Duke Huan thereby rose; Jin had the trouble of Lady Li yet Duke Wen thereby achieved hegemony."

sentences.zh: 近世趙王不終，諸呂作亂，而孝文為太宗。

translations.literal: In recent times the Prince of Zhao did not reach his end, the Lü clan made rebellion, yet Emperor Wen of Filial Piety became the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the Prince of Zhao did not reach his end, the Lü clan rebelled, yet Emperor Wen became the Grand Ancestor."

sentences.zh: 繇是觀之，禍亂之作，將以開聖人也。

translations.literal: From this to observe, the making of calamity and disorder is about to open the way for a sage.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that calamity and disorder are made to open the way for a sage."

sentences.zh: 夫繼變亂之後，必有異舊之恩，此賢聖所以昭天命也。

translations.literal: After inheriting change and disorder there must be favor unlike the old—this is how the worthy and sage display Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: After inheriting change and disorder there must be favor unlike the old—this is how the worthy and sage display Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 往者昭帝即世無嗣，昌邑淫亂，乃皇天所以開至聖也。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Zhao departed the world without an heir; Changyi was dissolute and disorderly—this was how August Heaven opened the way for the utmost sage.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Zhao died without an heir; Changyi was dissolute and disorderly—this was how August Heaven opened the way for the utmost sage."

sentences.zh: 臣聞《春秋》正即位、大一統而慎始也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies accession, unifies in the great, and is careful at the beginning.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that the Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies accession, unifies in the great, and is careful at the beginning."

sentences.zh: 陛下初登至尊，與天合符，宜改前世之失，正始受命之統，滌煩文，除民疾，以應天意。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has newly ascended the utmost honor and matches Heaven's talisman; you ought to change the former age's errors, rectify the beginning of receiving the mandate's succession, wash away vexatious documents, and remove the people's afflictions to respond to Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has newly ascended the throne and matches Heaven's talisman; you ought to change the former age's errors, rectify the beginning of receiving the mandate, wash away vexatious documents, and remove the people's afflictions to respond to Heaven's intent."

sentences.zh: 臣聞秦有十失，其一尚存，治獄之吏是也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Qin had ten failures; one still remains—the officers who govern prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that Qin had ten failures; one still remains—the officers who govern prisons."

sentences.zh: 夫獄者，天下之大命也，死者不可復生，絕者不可復屬。

translations.literal: For prisons are the great mandate of all under Heaven; the dead cannot live again, the severed cannot be rejoined.
translations.idiomatic: For prisons are the great mandate of the realm; the dead cannot live again, the severed cannot be rejoined."

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『與其殺不辜，寧失不經。

translations.literal: The Documents says: "Rather than execute the innocent, better to miss and not hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: "Rather than execute the innocent, better to miss and not hit the mark."

sentences.zh: 』今治獄吏則不然，上下相驅，以刻為明，深者獲公名，平者多後患，故治獄之吏皆欲人死，非憎人也，自安之道在人之死。

translations.literal: " Now officers who govern prisons are not so; above and below drive one another, taking harshness as clarity. The deep win public renown; the fair mostly suffer later trouble—therefore prison officers all wish men dead. It is not that they hate people; their path to security lies in men's death.
translations.idiomatic: " Now prison officers are not so; above and below drive one another, taking harshness as clarity. The harsh win public renown; the fair mostly suffer later trouble—therefore prison officers all wish men dead. It is not that they hate people; their path to security lies in men's death."

sentences.zh: 是以死人之血流離於市，被刑之徒，比肩而立，大辟之計，歲以萬數。

translations.literal: Therefore dead men's blood flows and pools in the markets; those bearing punishment stand shoulder to shoulder; reckonings of capital punishment number tens of thousands each year.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore dead men's blood pools in the markets; those bearing punishment stand shoulder to shoulder; capital sentences number in the tens of thousands each year."

sentences.zh: 此仁聖之所以傷也，太平之未洽，凡以此也。

translations.literal: This is what benevolence and sagehood grieve; that great peace is not yet thorough—all for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: This is what benevolence and sagehood grieve; that great peace is not yet thorough—all for this reason."

sentences.zh: 夫人情，安則樂生，痛則思死，棰楚之下，何求而不得！

translations.literal: For human feeling: when at ease one delights in life; when in pain one thinks of death. Under rod and cudgel, what could one seek and not obtain!
translations.idiomatic: Human nature: when at ease one delights in life; when in pain one thinks of death. Under rod and cudgel, what could one seek and not obtain!"

sentences.zh: 故囚人不勝痛，則飾辭以示之；

translations.literal: Therefore when a prisoner cannot bear the pain, he adorns his words to show them;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when a prisoner cannot bear the pain, he adorns his words to show them;

sentences.zh: 吏治者利其然，則指導以明之；

translations.literal: the officer who governs the case profits from this and guides him to make it clear;
translations.idiomatic: the officer who governs the case profits from this and guides him to make it clear;

sentences.zh: 上奏畏卻，則鍛練而周內之。

translations.literal: fearing rejection when memorializing upward, he forges and refines and wraps it tightly within.
translations.idiomatic: fearing rejection when memorializing upward, he forges and refines and wraps it tightly within.

sentences.zh: 蓋奏當之成，雖皋陶聽之，猶以為死有餘辜。

translations.literal: When a memorial on the sentence is complete, even if Gao Yao heard it, he would still think death left surplus guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When a memorial on the sentence is complete, even if Gao Yao heard it, he would still think death left surplus guilt.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 成練者眾，文致之罪明也。

translations.literal: Because those forged and refined are many, and the crime woven in words is clear.
translations.idiomatic: Because those forged and refined are many, and the crime woven in words is clear.

sentences.zh: 故俗語曰：『畫地為獄，議不入；

translations.literal: Therefore a common saying runs: "Draw the ground as a prison—argument will not enter;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a common saying runs: "Draw the ground as a prison—argument will not enter;"

sentences.zh: 刻木為吏，期不對。

translations.literal: carve wood as an officer—one would not answer even on appointment.
translations.idiomatic: carve wood as an officer—one would not answer even on appointment."

sentences.zh: 』此皆疾吏之風，悲痛之辭也。

translations.literal: " These are all the wind of hateful officers, words of grief and pain.
translations.idiomatic: " These are all the wind of hateful officers, words of grief and pain."

sentences.zh: 唯陛下省法制，寬刑罰，則太平之風可興於世。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty examines the legal system and relaxes punishments can the wind of great peace rise in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty examines the legal system and relaxes punishments can the wind of great peace rise in the age."

sentences.zh: 」上善其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: ----9十二月，詔曰：「間者吏用法巧文浸深，是朕之不德也。

translations.literal: ----9 In the twelfth month, an edict said: "Recently officers applying the law with crafty documents have grown ever deeper—this is Our lack of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 In the twelfth month, an edict said: "Recently officers applying the law with crafty documents have grown ever deeper—this is Our lack of virtue."

sentences.zh: 夫決獄不當，使有罪興邪，不辜蒙戮，父子悲恨，朕甚傷之！

translations.literal: When deciding prison cases is not correct, it makes the guilty rise in wickedness and the innocent suffer execution—fathers and sons grieve and resent; We are deeply grieved!
translations.idiomatic: When deciding prison cases is not correct, it makes the guilty rise in wickedness and the innocent suffer execution—fathers and sons grieve and resent; We are deeply grieved!"

sentences.zh: 今遣廷史與郡鞠獄，任輕祿薄，其為置廷尉平，秩六百石，員四人。

translations.literal: Now We send Court Clerks with commanderies to try prison cases; their duties are light and emoluments thin—let there be established Commandant of Justice Assessors, rank six hundred bushels, four posts.
translations.idiomatic: Now We send Court Clerks with commanderies to try prison cases; their duties are light and emoluments thin—let Commandant of Justice Assessors be established, rank six hundred bushels, four posts."

sentences.zh: 其務平之，以稱朕意！

translations.literal: Let them strive for fairness to match Our intent!
translations.idiomatic: Let them strive for fairness to match Our intent!"

sentences.zh: 」於是每季秋後請讞時，上常幸宣室，齋居而決事，獄刑號為平矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon each time after the autumn quarter when cases for review were submitted, the emperor often favored the Xuan Chamber, dwelt in fasting seclusion to decide affairs, and prison punishments were styled as fair.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon each autumn quarter when cases for review were submitted, the emperor often visited the Xuan Chamber, dwelt in fasting seclusion to decide affairs, and prison punishments were styled as fair.

sentences.zh: 涿郡太守鄭昌上疏言：「今明主躬垂明聽，雖不置廷平，獄將自正；

translations.literal: Governor of Zhuo commandery Zheng Chang submitted a memorial, saying: "Now the enlightened lord personally bends his clear hearing; though Assessors are not established, prisons will of themselves be rectified;
translations.idiomatic: Governor of Zhuo Zheng Chang submitted a memorial: "Now the enlightened lord personally bends his clear hearing; though Assessors are not established, prisons will of themselves be rectified;"

sentences.zh: 若開後嗣，不若刪定律令。

translations.literal: if one opens this for later successors, better to delete and fix laws and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: if one opens this for later successors, better to delete and fix laws and statutes."

sentences.zh: 律令一定，愚民知所避，奸吏無所弄矣。

translations.literal: Once laws and statutes are fixed, foolish commoners know what to avoid and wicked officials have nothing to manipulate.
translations.idiomatic: Once laws and statutes are fixed, foolish commoners know what to avoid and wicked officials have nothing to manipulate."

sentences.zh: 今不正其本，而置廷平以理其末，政衰聽怠，則廷平將召權而為亂首矣。

translations.literal: Now if one does not rectify the root but establishes Assessors to manage the branch, when government declines and hearing grows slack, Assessors will summon power and become leaders of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Now if one does not rectify the root but establishes Assessors to manage the branch, when government declines and hearing grows slack, Assessors will summon power and become leaders of disorder."

sentences.zh: 」----10昭帝時，匈奴使四千騎田車師。

translations.literal: " ----10 In Emperor Zhao's time, the Xiongnu sent four thousand horsemen to farm in Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: " ----10 In Emperor Zhao's reign, the Xiongnu sent four thousand horsemen to farm in Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 及五將軍擊匈奴，車師田者驚去，車師復通於漢；

translations.literal: When the Five Generals attacked the Xiongnu, those farming in Cheshi fled in alarm; Cheshi reopened relations with Han;
translations.idiomatic: When the Five Generals attacked the Xiongnu, the Cheshi farmers fled in alarm, and Cheshi reopened relations with Han;

sentences.zh: 匈奴怒，召其太子軍宿，欲以為質。

translations.literal: the Xiongnu were angry, summoned their heir Jun Su, and wished to take him as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: the Xiongnu were angry, summoned their heir Jun Su, and wished to take him as hostage.

sentences.zh: 軍宿，焉耆外孫，不欲質匈奴，亡走焉耆，車師王更立子烏貴為太子。

translations.literal: Jun Su, a grandson by the female line of Yanqi, did not wish to be a hostage to the Xiongnu, fled to Yanqi, and the King of Cheshi established his son Wu Gui as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Su, a maternal grandson of Yanqi, refused to be a hostage to the Xiongnu, fled to Yanqi, and the King of Cheshi made his son Wu Gui heir instead.

sentences.zh: 及烏貴立為王，與匈奴結婚姻，教匈奴遮漢道通烏孫者。

translations.literal: When Wu Gui was established as king, he formed a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu and taught the Xiongnu to block Han routes to Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Gui became king, he allied with the Xiongnu by marriage and taught them to block Han routes to Wusun.

sentences.zh: 是歲，侍郎會稽鄭吉與校尉司馬憙，將免刑罪人田渠犁，積穀，發城郭諸國兵萬餘人與所將田士千五百人共擊車師，破之；

translations.literal: That year, Gentleman Attendant Zheng Ji of Kuaiji and Commandant Si Ma Xi led convicts exempted from punishment to farm at Queli, accumulated grain, mobilized more than ten thousand troops from the walled-city states together with the fifteen hundred farming soldiers they led to jointly attack Cheshi and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: That year, Gentleman Attendant Zheng Ji of Kuaiji and Commandant Si Ma Xi led convicts farming at Queli, accumulated grain, and with more than ten thousand troops from the frontier states plus the fifteen hundred farming soldiers they led jointly attacked Cheshi and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 車師王請降。

translations.literal: The King of Cheshi requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Cheshi asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 匈奴發兵攻車師；

translations.literal: The Xiongnu dispatched troops to attack Cheshi;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu sent troops to attack Cheshi;

sentences.zh: 吉、憙引兵北逢之，匈奴不敢前。

translations.literal: Ji and Xi led troops north, encountered them, and the Xiongnu did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Xi led troops north, met them, and the Xiongnu did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 吉、憙即留一候與卒二十人留守王，吉等引兵歸渠犁。

translations.literal: Ji and Xi immediately left one scout with twenty soldiers to guard the king; Ji and the rest led troops back to Queli.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Xi left one scout with twenty soldiers to guard the king and led the rest back to Queli.

sentences.zh: 車師王恐匈奴兵復至而見殺也，乃輕騎奔烏孫。

translations.literal: The King of Cheshi feared Xiongnu troops would come again and he would be killed, so with light cavalry he fled to Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Cheshi, fearing the Xiongnu would return and kill him, fled on light cavalry to Wusun.

sentences.zh: 吉即迎其妻子，傳送長安。

translations.literal: Ji immediately welcomed his wife and children and sent them on to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ji welcomed his wife and children and sent them on to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 匈奴更以車師王昆弟兜莫為車師王，收其餘民東徙，不敢居故地；

translations.literal: The Xiongnu again installed the King's younger brother Dou Mo as King of Cheshi, gathered the remaining people and moved east, and did not dare dwell in the former territory;
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu installed the king's younger brother Dou Mo as King of Cheshi, gathered the remaining people and moved east, and did not dare remain in the old territory;

sentences.zh: 而鄭吉始使吏卒三百人往田車師地以實之。

translations.literal: while Zheng Ji for the first time sent three hundred clerks and soldiers to farm Cheshi territory to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: while Zheng Ji for the first time sent three hundred clerks and soldiers to farm Cheshi territory and settle it.

sentences.zh: ----11上自初即位，數遣使者求外家；

translations.literal: ----11 Since he first took the throne, the emperor repeatedly sent envoys to seek his maternal kin;
translations.idiomatic: ----11 From the time he first took the throne, the emperor repeatedly sent envoys to seek his maternal kin;

sentences.zh: 久遠，多似類而非是。

translations.literal: After long years, many resembled them but were not.
translations.idiomatic: After so long, many who resembled them proved not to be kin.

sentences.zh: 是歲，求得外祖母王媼及媼男無故、武。

translations.literal: That year he found his maternal grandmother Old Lady Wang and her sons Wugu and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: That year he found his maternal grandmother Old Lady Wang and her sons Wugu and Wu.

sentences.zh: 上賜無故、武爵關內侯。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed on Wugu and Wu the rank Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed on Wugu and Wu the rank of Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 旬月間，賞賜以巨萬計。

translations.literal: Within a month rewards tallied in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month rewards totaled in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，賜外祖母號為博平君；

translations.literal: 1 Spring, second month, he bestowed on his maternal grandmother the title Lady Bo Ping;
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the second month, he bestowed on his maternal grandmother the title Lady Bo Ping;

sentences.zh: 封舅無故為平昌侯，武為樂昌侯。

translations.literal: he enfeoffed his maternal uncle Wugu as Marquis of Pingchang and Wu as Marquis of Lechang.
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed his maternal uncle Wugu as Marquis of Pingchang and Wu as Marquis of Lechang.

sentences.zh: ----2夏，五月，山陽、濟陰雹如雞子，深二尺五寸，殺二十餘人，飛鳥皆死。

translations.literal: ----2 Summer, fifth month, in Shanyang and Jiyin hail like chicken eggs, two chi five cun deep, killed more than twenty people, and flying birds all died.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 In summer, the fifth month, hail like chicken eggs fell in Shanyang and Jiyin to a depth of two chi five cun, killing more than twenty people; all flying birds died.

sentences.zh: ----3詔：「自今子有匿父母、妻匿夫、孫匿大父母，皆勿治。

translations.literal: ----3 Edict: "From now on, if sons conceal parents, wives conceal husbands, or grandsons conceal grandparents, all shall not be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 Edict: "From now on, if sons conceal parents, wives conceal husbands, or grandsons conceal grandparents, none shall be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 」----4立廣川惠王孫文為廣川王。

translations.literal: " ----4 He established Wen, grandson of King Hui of Guangchuan, as King of Guangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: " ----4 He established Wen, grandson of King Hui of Guangchuan, as King of Guangchuan.

sentences.zh: ----5霍顯及禹、山、雲自見日侵削，數相對啼泣自怨。

translations.literal: ----5 Huo Xian and Yu, Shan, and Yun, seeing themselves daily eroded, repeatedly faced each other weeping and blaming themselves.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 Huo Xian and Yu, Shan, and Yun, seeing their power daily eroded, repeatedly faced each other weeping and blaming themselves.

sentences.zh: 山曰：「今丞相用事，縣官信之，盡變易大將軍時法令，發揚大將軍過失。

translations.literal: Shan said: "Now the chancellor holds power and the court trusts him; he has completely altered all laws and regulations from the Grand General's time and publicized the Grand General's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said, "Now the chancellor holds power and the court trusts him; he has completely overturned the Grand General's laws and publicized the Grand General's faults.

sentences.zh: 又，諸儒生多窶人子，遠客饑寒，喜妄說狂言，不避忌諱，大將軍常讎之。

translations.literal: Also, many Confucian scholars are sons of poor men, far-traveling guests hungry and cold, who delight in reckless wild speech and do not avoid taboo—the Grand General constantly resented them.
translations.idiomatic: Also, many Confucian scholars are poor men's sons, far-traveling guests hungry and cold, who delight in reckless speech and ignore taboo—the Grand General always resented them.

sentences.zh: 今陛下好與諸儒生語，人人自書對事，多言我家者。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty delights in speaking with the Confucian scholars; each man writes his own reply on affairs, and many speak of my house.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty delights in speaking with Confucian scholars; each writes his own reply on affairs, and many speak of our house.

sentences.zh: 嘗有上書言我家昆弟驕恣，其言絕痛；

translations.literal: Once there was a memorial saying our brothers were arrogant and wanton—the words were utterly harsh;
translations.idiomatic: Once a memorial said our brothers were arrogant and wanton—the words were utterly harsh;

sentences.zh: 山屏不奏。

translations.literal: Shan screened it and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Shan suppressed it and did not submit it.

sentences.zh: 後上書者益黠，盡奏封事，輒使中書令出取之，不關尚書，益不信人。

translations.literal: Later memorializers grew craftier; all submitted sealed reports, and the emperor would have the Director of the Palace Secretariat fetch them, not passing through the Directors of Writing, trusting people less and less.
translations.idiomatic: Later memorializers grew craftier; all submitted sealed reports, and the emperor had the Director of the Palace Secretariat fetch them without passing through the Directors of Writing, trusting people less and less.

sentences.zh: 又聞民間讙言『霍氏毒殺許皇后』，寧有是邪？

translations.literal: I also heard among the people rejoicing speech, 'The Huo clan poisoned and murdered Empress Xu'—could there be such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: I also heard among the people the cry, 'The Huo clan poisoned Empress Xu'—could there be such a thing?

sentences.zh: 」顯恐急，即具以實告禹、山、雲。

translations.literal: " Xian in fear and haste immediately told the full truth to Yu, Shan, and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian in fear and haste immediately told Yu, Shan, and Yun the full truth.

sentences.zh: 禹、山、雲驚曰：「如是，何不早告禹等！

translations.literal: Yu, Shan, and Yun in alarm said: "If so, why did you not tell us earlier!
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Shan, and Yun cried in alarm, "If so, why did you not tell us earlier!

sentences.zh: 縣官離散、斥逐諸婿，用是故也。

translations.literal: The court dismissing and expelling all the sons-in-law—this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The court's dismissal and expulsion of all the sons-in-law—that was the reason.

sentences.zh: 此大事，誅罰不小，奈何？

translations.literal: This is a great matter; the punishment will not be small—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: This is a grave matter; the punishment will be severe—what can we do?

sentences.zh: 」於是始有邪謀矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they first had wicked plotting.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they first turned to wicked plotting.

sentences.zh: 雲舅李竟民善張赦，見雲家卒卒，謂竟曰：「今丞相與平恩侯用事，可令太夫人言太后，先誅此兩人。

translations.literal: Yun's maternal uncle Li Jing, a commoner skilled with Zhang She, seeing the Yun household in sudden distress, said to Jing: "Now the chancellor and Marquis of Ping'en hold power—you can have the Grand Lady speak to the Empress Dowager and first execute these two men.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's maternal uncle Li Jing, a commoner friendly with Zhang She, seeing the Yun household in sudden distress, said to Jing, "Now the chancellor and Marquis of Ping'en hold power—have the Grand Lady speak to the Empress Dowager and first execute these two men.

sentences.zh: 移徙陛下，在太后耳。

translations.literal: Removing and relocating Your Majesty rests with the Empress Dowager alone.
translations.idiomatic: Removing the emperor rests with the Empress Dowager alone.

sentences.zh: 」長安男子張章告之，事下廷尉、執金吾，捕張赦等。

translations.literal: " A man of Chang'an named Zhang Zhang reported it; the matter was sent down to the Commandant of Justice and Commandant of the Capital Guard to arrest Zhang She and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: " A Chang'an man named Zhang Zhang reported it; the matter went to the Commandant of Justice and Commandant of the Capital Guard to arrest Zhang She and the rest.

sentences.zh: 後有詔，止勿捕。

translations.literal: Later there was an edict ordering them to stop and not arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict ordered them to stop and not arrest.

sentences.zh: 山等愈恐，相謂曰：「此縣官重太后，故不竟也。

translations.literal: Shan and the rest grew more fearful and said to each other: "The court esteems the Empress Dowager, therefore it did not carry through.
translations.idiomatic: Shan and the rest grew more fearful and said to each other, "The court esteems the Empress Dowager, so it did not carry through.

sentences.zh: 然惡端已見，久之猶發，發即族矣，不如先也。

translations.literal: Yet the evil root is already visible; if after long it still breaks out, when it breaks out the clan will be exterminated—better to strike first.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the evil is already visible; if it breaks out later, the whole clan will be exterminated—better to strike first.

sentences.zh: 」遂令諸女各歸報其夫，皆曰：「安所相避！

translations.literal: " Thereupon they ordered each daughter to return and report to her husband; all said: "Where is there mutual avoidance!
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon they ordered each daughter to return and report to her husband; all said, "Where is there any avoiding one another!

sentences.zh: 會李竟坐與諸侯王交通，辭語及霍氏，有詔：「雲、山不宜宿衛，免就第。

translations.literal: Just then Li Jing was convicted of communicating with kings and princes of feudatory states; his testimony touched the Huo clan. There was an edict: "Yun and Shan are unfit for palace guard duty; dismissed to their estates.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Li Jing was convicted of communicating with feudatory kings; his testimony implicated the Huo clan. An edict said, "Yun and Shan are unfit for palace guard duty; dismissed to their estates.

sentences.zh: 」山陽太守張敞上封事曰：「臣聞公子季友有功於魯，趙衰有功於晉，田完有功於齊，皆疇其庸，延及子孫。

translations.literal: " Governor of Shanyang Zhang Chang submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that Duke Ji You of Lu, Zhao Cui of Jin, and Tian Wan of Qi all had merit for their states, and each was rewarded for his service, extending to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: " Governor of Shanyang Zhang Chang submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "Your servant has heard that Ji You of Lu, Zhao Cui of Jin, and Tian Wan of Qi all had merit for their states, were rewarded for their service, and their rewards extended to their descendants.

sentences.zh: 終後田氏篡齊，趙氏分晉，季氏顓魯。

translations.literal: In the end afterward the house of Tian usurped Qi, the house of Zhao partitioned Jin, and the house of Ji dominated Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the house of Tian usurped Qi, the house of Zhao partitioned Jin, and the house of Ji dominated Lu.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼作《春秋》，跡盛衰，譏世卿最甚。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, tracing rise and decline, reproaching hereditary ministers most severely.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, tracing rise and decline and reproaching hereditary ministers most severely.

sentences.zh: 乃者大將軍決大計，安宗廟，定天下，功亦不細矣。

translations.literal: Recently the Grand General decided great plans, secured the ancestral temple, and settled all under Heaven—his merit is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Grand General decided great plans, secured the ancestral temple, and settled the realm—his merit is not slight.

sentences.zh: 夫周公七年耳，而大將軍二十歲，海內之命斷於掌握。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou held power seven years, whereas the Grand General held it twenty years, and the realm's commands rested in his grasp.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou held power seven years, whereas the Grand General held it twenty years, and the realm's commands rested in his grasp.

sentences.zh: 方其隆盛時，感動天地，侵迫陰陽。

translations.literal: At the height of his grandeur he moved Heaven and Earth and encroached upon yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: At the height of his power he moved Heaven and Earth and encroached upon yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 朝臣宜有明言曰：『陛下褒寵故大將軍以報功德足矣。

translations.literal: Court ministers ought to have spoken plainly, saying: 'Your Majesty's favor and reward of the former Grand General to repay his merit is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers ought to have spoken plainly, saying, 'Your Majesty's favor and reward of the former Grand General to repay his merit is enough.

sentences.zh: 間者輔臣顓政，貴戚太盛，君臣之分不明，請罷霍氏三侯皆就第；

translations.literal: Recently assisting ministers have monopolized government, noble kin are too powerful, and the distinction between ruler and minister is unclear—we request that the three Huo marquises all retire to their estates;
translations.idiomatic: Recently assisting ministers have monopolized government, noble kin are too powerful, and the distinction between ruler and minister is unclear—we ask that the three Huo marquises retire to their estates;

sentences.zh: 及衛將軍張安世，宜賜-{几}-杖歸休，時存問召見，以列侯為天子師。

translations.literal: and Guardian General Zhang Anshi ought to be bestowed a {-几}- bench and staff to retire, with occasional inquiries and summons to audience, serving as the Son of Heaven's teacher in the capacity of a ranked marquis.
translations.idiomatic: and Guardian General Zhang Anshi ought to be bestowed a bench and staff to retire, with occasional inquiries and summons to audience, serving as the emperor's teacher in the capacity of a ranked marquis.

sentences.zh: 』明詔以恩不聽，群臣以義固爭而後許之，天下必以陛下為不忘功德而朝臣為知禮，霍氏世世無所患苦。

translations.literal: ' A clear edict in grace would not heed it; the assembled ministers would firmly contend on principle and only afterward obtain assent—the realm would surely take Your Majesty as not forgetting merit and the court ministers as knowing ritual, and the Huo clan for generations would have no affliction.
translations.idiomatic: ' A clear edict in grace would not heed it; the ministers would firmly contend on principle and only afterward obtain assent—the realm would surely see Your Majesty as not forgetting merit and the court ministers as knowing ritual, and the Huo clan for generations would have no affliction.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷不聞直聲，而令明詔自親其文，非策之得者也。

translations.literal: Now the court hears no forthright voice, yet has a clear edict personally draft its text—this is not a policy that succeeds.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court hears no forthright voice, yet has a clear edict personally draft its text—this is not sound policy.

sentences.zh: 今兩侯已出，人情不相遠，以臣心度之，大司馬及其枝屬必有畏懼之心。

translations.literal: Now the two marquises have been removed; human feelings are not far apart—in your servant's estimation, the Grand Marshal and his branch kin must have hearts of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Now the two marquises have been removed; human feelings are not far apart—in your servant's judgment, the Grand Marshal and his kin must be fearful.

sentences.zh: 夫近臣自危，非完計也。

translations.literal: When close ministers feel themselves endangered, it is not a complete plan.
translations.idiomatic: When close ministers feel endangered, it is not a sound plan.

sentences.zh: 臣敞願於廣朝白發其端，直守遠郡，其路無由。

translations.literal: Your servant Chang wishes to speak plainly in broad court and disclose its root, yet holding a distant commandery, there is no way.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Chang wishes to speak plainly in open court and disclose its root, yet holding a distant commandery, has no way to do so.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下省察。

translations.literal: I pray only that Your Majesty examine this.
translations.idiomatic: I pray only that Your Majesty examine this.

sentences.zh: 」上甚善其計，然不召也。

translations.literal: " The emperor greatly approved his plan, yet did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor greatly approved his plan, yet did not summon him.

sentences.zh: 禹、山等家數有妖怪，舉家憂愁。

translations.literal: In the households of Yu, Shan, and the rest there were several portents; the whole family was anxious and sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: In the households of Yu, Shan, and the rest there were several portents; the whole family was anxious and sorrowful.

sentences.zh: 山曰：「丞相擅減宗廟羔、菟、蛙，可以此罪也。

translations.literal: Shan said: "The chancellor on his own authority reduced the ancestral temple's lambs, rabbits, and frogs—we can use this as a charge.
translations.idiomatic: Shan said, "The chancellor on his own authority reduced the ancestral temple's lambs, rabbits, and frogs—we can use this as a charge.

sentences.zh: 」謀令太后為博平君置酒，召丞相、平恩侯以下，使范明友、鄧廣漢承太后制引斬之，因廢天子而立禹。

translations.literal: " They plotted to have the Empress Dowager hold a banquet for Lady Bo Ping, summon the chancellor, Marquis of Ping'en, and those below, and have Fan Mingyou and Deng Guanghan act on the Empress Dowager's command to lead them out and behead them, then depose the Son of Heaven and establish Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " They plotted to have the Empress Dowager hold a banquet for Lady Bo Ping, summon the chancellor, Marquis of Ping'en, and those below, and have Fan Mingyou and Deng Guanghan act on the Empress Dowager's command to lead them out and behead them, then depose the emperor and establish Yu.

sentences.zh: 約定，未發，雲拜為玄菟太守，太中大夫任宣為代郡太守。

translations.literal: The agreement was made but not yet launched; Yun was appointed Governor of Xuantu and Grandee of the Palace Ren Xuan was appointed Governor of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The agreement was made but not yet launched; Yun was appointed Governor of Xuantu and Palace Grandee Ren Xuan was appointed Governor of Dai.

sentences.zh: 會事發覺，秋，七月，雲、山、明友自殺，顯、禹、廣漢等捕得；

translations.literal: Just then the affair was discovered. Autumn, seventh month: Yun, Shan, and Mingyou killed themselves; Xian, Yu, Guanghan, and the rest were captured;
translations.idiomatic: Just then the affair was discovered. In autumn, the seventh month, Yun, Shan, and Mingyou killed themselves; Xian, Yu, Guanghan, and the rest were captured;

sentences.zh: 禹要斬，顯及諸女昆弟皆棄市；

translations.literal: Yu was beheaded at the waist; Xian and all the daughters and brothers were executed in the market;
translations.idiomatic: Yu was beheaded at the waist; Xian and all the daughters and brothers were executed in the market;

sentences.zh: 與霍氏相連坐誅滅者數十家。

translations.literal: those implicated with the Huo clan and jointly punished by extermination numbered several tens of households.
translations.idiomatic: several tens of households implicated with the Huo clan were jointly exterminated.

sentences.zh: 太僕杜延年以霍氏舊人，亦坐免官。

translations.literal: Grand Master of Studs Du Yannian, as an old associate of the Huo clan, was also convicted and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of Studs Du Yannian, as an old associate of the Huo clan, was also convicted and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 八月，己酉，皇后霍氏廢，處昭台宮，乙丑，詔封告霍氏反謀者男子張章、期門董忠、左曹楊惲、侍中金安上、史高皆為列侯。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiyou: Empress Huo was deposed and placed in Zhaotai Palace. Day yichou: an edict enfeoffed as ranked marquises the men who reported the Huo clan's rebellion—Zhang Zhang, Barrier Gate Dong Zhong, Left Censor-in-Chief Yang Yun, Palace Attendant Jin Anshang, and Shi Gao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on day jiyou, Empress Huo was deposed and placed in Zhaotai Palace. On day yichou, an edict enfeoffed as ranked marquises Zhang Zhang, Barrier Gate Dong Zhong, Left Censor-in-Chief Yang Yun, Palace Attendant Jin Anshang, and Shi Gao, who had reported the Huo rebellion.

sentences.zh: 惲，丞相敞子；

translations.literal: Yun was Chancellor Chang's son;
translations.idiomatic: Yun was Chancellor Chang's son;

sentences.zh: 安上，車騎將軍日磾弟子；

translations.literal: Anshang was Cavalry-and-Chariots General Rizhu's nephew;
translations.idiomatic: Anshang was Cavalry-and-Chariots General Rizhu's nephew;

sentences.zh: 高，史良娣兄子也。

translations.literal: Gao was Lady Shi Liangdi's brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was Lady Shi Liangdi's brother's son.

sentences.zh: 初，霍氏奢侈，茂陵徐生曰：「霍氏必亡。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Huo clan was extravagant; Xu Sheng of Maoling said: "The Huo clan will surely perish.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Huo clan was extravagant; Xu Sheng of Maoling said, "The Huo clan will surely perish.

sentences.zh: 夫奢則不遜，不遜則侮上。

translations.literal: Extravagance leads to lack of deference; lack of deference leads to insulting one's superior.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagance leads to lack of deference; lack of deference leads to insulting one's superior.

sentences.zh: 侮上者，逆道也，在人之右，眾必害之。

translations.literal: One who insults his superior violates the Way; standing to men's right, the multitude will surely harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Insulting one's superior violates the Way; standing above others, the multitude will surely harm you.

sentences.zh: 霍氏秉權日久，害之者多矣。

translations.literal: The Huo clan has held power long; those who would harm them are many.
translations.idiomatic: The Huo clan has held power long; those who would harm them are many.

sentences.zh: 天下害之，而又行以逆道，不亡何待！

translations.literal: All under Heaven would harm them, and they also act by the rebellious Way—if they do not perish, what are we waiting for!
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven would harm them, and they also act rebelliously—if they do not perish, what are we waiting for!

sentences.zh: 」乃上疏言：「霍氏泰盛，陛下即愛厚之，宜以時抑制，無使至亡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial, saying: "The Huo clan is excessively grand; even if Your Majesty loves and favors them, you ought in good time to restrain them and not let them reach ruin.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he submitted a memorial, saying, "The Huo clan is excessively powerful; even if Your Majesty loves and favors them, you ought in good time to restrain them and not let them reach ruin.

sentences.zh: 」書三上，輒報聞。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted three times; each time the reply was merely 'noted.'
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted three times; each time the reply was merely noted.

sentences.zh: 其後霍氏誅滅，而告霍氏者皆封，人為徐生上書曰：「臣聞客有過主人者，見其灶直突，傍有積薪，客謂主人：『更為曲突，遠徙其薪，不者且有火患。

translations.literal: Afterward the Huo clan was exterminated and those who reported the Huo clan were all enfeoffed; a man submitted a memorial on Xu Sheng's behalf, saying: "Your servant has heard that a guest who visited his host saw the stove with a straight chimney and piled firewood beside it. The guest said to the host: 'Bend the chimney and move the firewood far away, or else there will soon be a fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Huo clan was exterminated and those who reported them were all enfeoffed; a man submitted a memorial on Xu Sheng's behalf, saying, "Your servant has heard that a guest visiting his host saw the stove with a straight chimney and piled firewood beside it. The guest said to the host, 'Bend the chimney and move the firewood far away, or there will soon be a fire.

sentences.zh: 』主人嘿然不應。

translations.literal: ' The host murmured assent but did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: ' The host murmured but did not respond.

sentences.zh: 俄而家果失火，鄰里共救之，幸而得息。

translations.literal: Before long the house indeed caught fire; neighbors jointly rescued it and by luck were able to extinguish it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the house indeed caught fire; neighbors jointly rescued it and by luck extinguished it.

sentences.zh: 於是殺牛置酒，謝其鄰人，灼爛者在於上行，餘各以功次坐，而不錄言曲突者。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed an ox and set out wine to thank his neighbors; those with scorched heads sat in the upper places, the rest each sat by merit in order, but he did not record the one who spoke of bending the chimney.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he killed an ox and set out wine to thank his neighbors; those with scorched heads sat in the upper places, the rest by merit in order, but he did not reward the one who spoke of bending the chimney.

sentences.zh: 人謂主人曰：『鄉使聽客之言，不費牛酒，終亡火患。

translations.literal: Someone said to the host: 'If you had earlier heeded the guest's words, you would not have spent ox and wine and would ultimately have had no fire disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to the host, 'If you had earlier heeded the guest's words, you would not have spent ox and wine and would ultimately have had no fire.

sentences.zh: 今論功而請賓，曲突徙薪無恩澤，焦頭爛額為上客邪？

translations.literal: Now in discussing merit and treating guests, bending the chimney and moving firewood receives no favor, while scorched heads and burned brows are honored guests?'
translations.idiomatic: Now in rewarding merit and treating guests, bending the chimney and moving firewood receives no favor, while scorched heads and burned brows are honored guests?'

sentences.zh: 』主人乃寤而請之。

translations.literal: ' The host thereupon awoke and invited him.
translations.idiomatic: ' The host thereupon understood and invited him.

sentences.zh: 今茂陵徐福，數上書言霍氏且有變，宜防絕之。

translations.literal: Now Xu Fu of Maoling repeatedly submitted memorials saying the Huo clan would soon have a change and ought to be prevented and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Now Xu Fu of Maoling repeatedly submitted memorials saying the Huo clan would soon rebel and ought to be prevented.

sentences.zh: 鄉使福說得行，則國無裂土出爵之費，臣無逆亂誅滅之敗。

translations.literal: If earlier Fu's counsel had been carried out, the state would have had no expense of carving territory and issuing ranks, and your servants would have had no disaster of rebellion and extermination.
translations.idiomatic: If earlier Fu's counsel had been carried out, the state would have had no expense of carving territory and issuing ranks, and your servants would have had no disaster of rebellion and extermination.

sentences.zh: 往事既已，而福獨不蒙其功，唯陛下察之，貴徙薪曲突之策，使居焦髮灼爛之右。

translations.literal: Past affairs are already done, yet Fu alone did not receive reward for his merit—I pray only that Your Majesty examine this, value the policy of moving firewood and bending the chimney, and place it above scorched hair and burned flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Past affairs are already done, yet Fu alone received no reward—I pray Your Majesty examine this, value the policy of moving firewood and bending the chimney, and place it above scorched hair and burned flesh.

sentences.zh: 」上乃賜福帛十匹，後以為郎。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon bestowed on Fu ten bolts of silk and later made him a Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor bestowed on Fu ten bolts of silk and later made him a Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 帝初立，謁見高廟，大將軍光驂乘，上內嚴憚之，若有芒刺在背。

translations.literal: When the emperor first took the throne and paid court at the High Temple, Grand General Guang rode beside him in the carriage; inwardly the emperor was sternly in awe of him, as if thorns were in his back.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first took the throne and paid court at the High Temple, Grand General Guang rode beside him in the carriage; inwardly the emperor was in awe of him, as if thorns were in his back.

sentences.zh: 後車騎將軍張安世代光驂乘，天子從容肆體，甚安近焉。

translations.literal: Later Cavalry-and-Chariots General Zhang Anshi replaced Guang riding beside him; the Son of Heaven was at ease and relaxed his body, very comfortable and close.
translations.idiomatic: Later Cavalry-and-Chariots General Zhang Anshi replaced Guang riding beside him; the emperor was at ease and relaxed, very comfortable and close.

sentences.zh: 及光身死而宗族竟誅，故俗傳霍氏之禍萌於驂乘。

translations.literal: When Guang died in person and the clan was ultimately exterminated, therefore popular tradition says the Huo clan's disaster sprouted from riding beside the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang died and the clan was ultimately exterminated, popular tradition says the Huo clan's disaster sprouted from riding beside the carriage.

sentences.zh: 後十二歲，霍-{后}-復徙雲林館，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Twelve years later, Huo-{后}- was again relocated to Yunlin Lodge and thereupon killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later, Empress Huo was again relocated to Yunlin Lodge and thereupon killed herself.

sentences.zh: :班固贊曰：霍光受襁褓之托，任漢室之寄，匡國家，安社稷，擁昭，立宣，雖周公、阿衡何以加此！

translations.literal: : Ban Gu's eulogy says: Huo Guang received the entrustment of the swaddling-clothes age and bore the Han house's commission; he rectified the state, secured the altars of soil and grain, enthroned Zhao, and established Xuan—even the Duke of Zhou and Ah Heng—how could they surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: : Ban Gu's eulogy says: Huo Guang received the entrustment of the infant heir and bore the Han house's commission; he rectified the state, secured the realm, enthroned Zhao, and established Xuan—even the Duke of Zhou and Yi Yin—how could they surpass this!

sentences.zh: 然光不學亡術，闇於大理；

translations.literal: Yet Guang did not study and lacked method; he was dark to great principle;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guang did not study and lacked method; he was blind to great principle;

sentences.zh: 陰妻邪謀，立女為-{后}-，湛溺盈溢之欲，以增顛覆之禍，死財三年，宗族誅夷，哀哉！

translations.literal: his wife secretly plotted wickedly, established his daughter as {后}-, steeped and drowned in overflowing desire, thereby increasing the disaster of overturning; three years after his death the clan was exterminated—alas!
translations.idiomatic: his wife secretly plotted wickedly, established his daughter as empress, steeped in overflowing desire, thereby increasing the disaster of overturning; three years after his death the clan was exterminated—alas!

sentences.zh: :臣光曰：霍光之輔漢室，可謂忠矣；

translations.literal: : Your servant Guang says: Huo Guang's assisting the Han house may be called loyal;
translations.idiomatic: : Your servant Guang says: Huo Guang's assisting the Han house may be called loyal;

sentences.zh: 然卒不能庇其宗，何也？

translations.literal: yet in the end he could not protect his clan—why?
translations.idiomatic: yet in the end he could not protect his clan—why?

sentences.zh: 夫威福者，人君之器也。

translations.literal: Authority and favor are the sovereign's instruments.
translations.idiomatic: Authority and favor are the sovereign's instruments.

sentences.zh: 人臣執之，久而不歸，鮮不及矣。

translations.literal: When ministers hold them and long do not return them, few fail to come to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers hold them and long fail to return them, few escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 以孝昭之明，十四而知上官桀之詐，固可以親政矣，況孝宣十九即位，聰明剛毅，知民疾苦，而光久專大柄，不知避去，多置私黨，充塞朝廷，使人主蓄憤於上，吏民積怨於下，切齒側目，待時而發，其得免於身幸矣，況子孫以驕侈趣之哉！

translations.literal: With Emperor Zhao of Filial Piety's clarity—at fourteen knowing Shangguan Jie's deceit—he surely could have personally governed; how much more Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety, who at nineteen took the throne, was intelligent, resolute, and knew the people's hardships—yet Guang long monopolized the great handle, did not know to withdraw, placed many private partisans filling the court, made the lord above store anger, officials and people below accumulate resentment, gnashing teeth and casting sidelong glances, waiting for the time to strike; that he escaped with his person was luck—how much more when sons and grandsons were driven toward arrogance and extravagance!
translations.idiomatic: With Emperor Zhao's clarity—at fourteen he knew Shangguan Jie's deceit—he surely could have governed in person; how much more Emperor Xuan, who took the throne at nineteen, was intelligent, resolute, and knew the people's hardships—yet Guang long monopolized power, did not know to withdraw, placed many private partisans who filled the court, made the ruler above store anger and officials and people below accumulate resentment, gnashing teeth and watching sidelong, waiting for the moment to strike; that he escaped with his life was luck—how much more when sons and grandsons were driven toward arrogance and extravagance!

sentences.zh: 雖然，向使孝宣專以祿秩賞賜富其子孫，使之食大縣，奉朝請，亦足以報盛德矣；

translations.literal: Even so, had Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety solely used salary ranks, rewards, and gifts to enrich his sons and grandsons, had them eat great counties, and attend court audiences, that would also have been enough to repay his great virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Even so, had Emperor Xuan solely used salaries, rewards, and gifts to enrich his sons and grandsons, had them hold great counties and attend court audiences, that would have been enough to repay his great virtue;

sentences.zh: 乃復任之以政，授之以兵，及事叢衅積，更加裁奪，遂至怨懼以生邪謀，豈徒霍氏之自禍哉？

translations.literal: yet he again entrusted them with government and handed them troops; when affairs piled up and grievances accumulated and he further cut and seized, it reached the point that resentment and fear bred wicked plots—is it only the Huo clan's self-brought disaster?
translations.idiomatic: yet he again entrusted them with government and handed them troops; when affairs piled up and grievances accumulated and he further cut and seized their power, resentment and fear bred wicked plots—is it only the Huo clan's self-brought disaster?

sentences.zh: 亦孝宣醞釀以成之也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety also brewed and completed it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan also brewed and brought it about.

sentences.zh: 昔鬬椒作亂於楚，莊王滅其族而赦箴尹克黃，以為子文無後，何以勸善。

translations.literal: Formerly Dou Jiao made rebellion in Chu; King Zhuang exterminated his clan yet pardoned Supervisor of the Girdle Ke Huang, thinking that with Ziwen having no posterity, how could one encourage good.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Dou Jiao rebelled in Chu; King Zhuang exterminated his clan yet pardoned Supervisor of the Girdle Ke Huang, reasoning that with Ziwen having no posterity, how could one encourage good.

sentences.zh: 夫以顯、禹、雲、山之罪，雖應夷滅，而光之忠勳不可不祀；

translations.literal: For the offenses of Xian, Yu, Yun, and Shan, though they deserved extermination to the last, Guang's loyal merit could not go unhonored;
translations.idiomatic: For the offenses of Xian, Yu, Yun, and Shan, though they deserved extermination to the last, Guang's loyal merit could not go unhonored;

sentences.zh: 遂使家無噍類，孝宣亦少恩哉！

translations.literal: yet he made the family without a mouthful left—Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety was also sparing in grace!
translations.idiomatic: yet he left not a mouthful in the family—Emperor Xuan was also sparing in grace!

sentences.zh: ----6九月，詔減天下鹽賈。

translations.literal: ----6 In the ninth month, an edict reduced salt merchants throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 In the ninth month, an edict reduced salt merchants throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 又令郡國歲上系囚以掠笞若瘐死者，所坐縣、名、爵、-{里}-，丞相、御史課殿最以聞。

translations.literal: He also ordered the commanderies and states yearly to report prisoners held who died from flogging or from illness in custody, with the county of offense, name, rank, and -{里}-; the chancellor and censor graded palace and worst and reported.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the commanderies and states yearly to report prisoners who died from flogging or illness in custody, with the county of offense, name, rank, and -{里}-; the chancellor and censor graded them and reported.

sentences.zh: ----7十二月，清河王年坐內亂廢，遷房陵。

translations.literal: ----7 In the twelfth month, the King of Qinghe, Nian, was deposed for internal disorder and moved to Fangling.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 In the twelfth month, the King of Qinghe, Nian, was deposed for internal disorder and moved to Fangling.

sentences.zh: ----8是歲，北海太守廬江朱邑以治行第一入為大司農，勃海太守龔遂入為水衡都尉。

translations.literal: ----8 That year, Zhu Yi of Lujiang, Governor of Beihai, entered office as Grand Minister of Agriculture for foremost governance, and Gong Sui, Governor of Bohai, entered as Colonel of the Water Balance.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 That year, Zhu Yi of Lujiang, Governor of Beihai, entered office as Grand Minister of Agriculture for foremost governance, and Gong Sui, Governor of Bohai, entered as Colonel of the Water Balance.

sentences.zh: 先是，勃海左右郡歲饑，盜賊並起，二千石不能禽制。

translations.literal: Earlier, the commanderies left and right of Bohai yearly suffered famine; bandits arose together, and the two-thousand-bushel officials could not capture and control them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the commanderies around Bohai yearly suffered famine; bandits arose together, and the governors could not capture and control them.

sentences.zh: 上選能治者，丞相、御史舉故昌邑郎中令龔遂，上拜為勃海太守。

translations.literal: The emperor selected one who could govern; the chancellor and censor recommended the former Chamberlain of the Palace of Changyi, Gong Sui, and the emperor appointed him Governor of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor selected one who could govern; the chancellor and censor recommended the former Chamberlain of the Palace of Changyi, Gong Sui, and the emperor appointed him Governor of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 召見，問：「何以治勃海，息其盜賊？

translations.literal: He was summoned and seen; the emperor asked: "By what means will you govern Bohai and quiet its bandits?
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and asked, "By what means will you govern Bohai and quiet its bandits?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「海瀕遐遠，不沾聖化，其民困於饑寒而吏不恤，故使陛下赤子盜弄陛下之兵於潢池中耳。

translations.literal: " He replied: "The sea's edge is remote and far, untouched by sagely transformation; its people are distressed by hunger and cold while officials do not pity them—therefore Your Majesty's red infants play with Your Majesty's troops in the muddy pool.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "The seacoast is remote and far, untouched by sagely transformation; its people suffer hunger and cold while officials do not pity them—therefore Your Majesty's own children play with Your Majesty's troops in the muddy pool.

sentences.zh: 今欲使臣勝之邪，將安之也？

translations.literal: Now does Your Majesty wish your subject to defeat them, or to settle them?
translations.idiomatic: Now does Your Majesty wish your subject to defeat them, or to settle them?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「選用賢良，固欲安之也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "In selecting and employing the worthy and good, I surely wish to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "In selecting and employing the worthy and good, I surely wish to settle them.

sentences.zh: 」遂曰：「臣聞治亂民猶治亂繩，不可急也；

translations.literal: " Sui said: "Your subject has heard that governing chaotic people is like governing a tangled rope—it cannot be hurried;
translations.idiomatic: " Sui said, "Your subject has heard that governing chaotic people is like untangling a rope—it cannot be hurried;

sentences.zh: 唯緩之，然後可治。

translations.literal: only by easing it can it then be governed.
translations.idiomatic: only by easing it can it then be governed.

sentences.zh: 臣願丞相、御史且無拘臣以文法，得一切便宜從事。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes the chancellor and censor for the time being not to bind your subject with written law, and to obtain leave to act expediently in all matters.
