translations.idiomatic: Your subject asks the chancellor and censor for the time being not to bind your subject with written law, and to be allowed to act expediently in all matters.

sentences.zh: 」上許焉，加賜黃金贈遣。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved, additionally bestowed gold, and sent him off with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved, additionally bestowed gold, and sent him off with gifts.

sentences.zh: 乘傳至勃海界，郡聞新太守至，發兵以迎。

translations.literal: Riding the relay carriage to Bohai's border, the commandery hearing the new governor had arrived, raised troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the relay carriage to Bohai's border, the commandery hearing the new governor had arrived, raised troops to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 遂皆遣還。

translations.literal: Sui sent them all back.
translations.idiomatic: Sui sent them all back.

sentences.zh: 移書敕屬縣：「悉罷逐捕盜賊吏，諸持鍺、鉤、田器者皆為良民，吏毋得問；

translations.literal: He sent a letter ordering the subordinate counties: "Entirely dismiss the officers who pursue and capture bandits; all who hold hoes, hooks, and field tools are good people—officers must not question them;
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter ordering the subordinate counties, "Entirely dismiss the officers who pursue and capture bandits; all who hold hoes, hooks, and field tools are good people—officers must not question them;

sentences.zh: 持兵者乃為賊。

translations.literal: those who hold weapons are the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: those who hold weapons are the bandits.

sentences.zh: 」遂單車獨行至府。

translations.literal: " Sui alone in a single carriage went alone to the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: " Sui alone in a single carriage went to the headquarters.

sentences.zh: 盜賊聞遂教令，即時解散，棄其兵弩而持鉤、鋤，於是悉平，民安土樂業。

translations.literal: The bandits hearing Sui's teaching and orders immediately dispersed, abandoned their crossbows and weapons and took hooks and hoes; thereupon all was pacified, and the people were secure on their land and delighted in their work.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits hearing Sui's orders immediately dispersed, abandoned their crossbows and weapons and took hooks and hoes; thereupon all was pacified, and the people were secure on their land and delighted in their work.

sentences.zh: 遂乃開倉廩假貧民，選用良吏尉安牧養焉。

translations.literal: Sui thereupon opened the granaries and lent to the poor, selected and employed good officials to comfort, settle, and nurture them.
translations.idiomatic: Sui thereupon opened the granaries and lent to the poor, selected and employed good officials to comfort, settle, and nurture them.

sentences.zh: 遂見齊俗奢侈，好末技，不田作，乃躬率以儉約，勸民務農桑，各以口率種樹畜養。

translations.literal: Sui saw Qi customs were extravagant, fond of secondary crafts, and did not till; he thereupon personally led with frugality, urged the people to devote themselves to farming and sericulture, and each according to mouths led in planting trees and raising livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Sui saw Qi customs were extravagant, fond of secondary crafts, and did not till; he thereupon personally led with frugality, urged the people to devote themselves to farming and sericulture, and each household planted trees and raised livestock according to its mouths.

sentences.zh: 民有帶持刀劍者，使賣劍買牛，賣刀買犢，曰：「何為帶牛佩犢！

translations.literal: Where people wore swords and blades, he had them sell swords to buy oxen and sell knives to buy calves, saying: "Why wear an ox and hang a calf!
translations.idiomatic: Where people wore swords and blades, he had them sell swords to buy oxen and sell knives to buy calves, saying, "Why wear an ox and hang a calf!

sentences.zh: 」勞來循行，郡中皆有畜積，獄訟止息。

translations.literal: " He comforted and came and went on inspection; throughout the commandery all had stored accumulations, and prison suits ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " He comforted them and went about on inspection; throughout the commandery all had stores, and litigation ceased.

sentences.zh: ----9烏孫公主女為龜茲王絳賓夫人。

translations.literal: ----9 The Wusun princess's daughter became the consort of the King of Kucha, Jiangbin.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 The Wusun princess's daughter became the consort of the King of Kucha, Jiangbin.

sentences.zh: 絳賓上書言：「得尚漢外孫，願與公主女俱入朝。

translations.literal: Jiangbin memorialized, saying: "Having obtained in marriage Han's outer granddaughter, I wish together with the princess's daughter to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangbin memorialized, "Having obtained in marriage Han's outer granddaughter, I wish together with the princess's daughter to enter court.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，龜茲王及其夫人來朝；

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, the King of Kucha and his consort came to court;
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, the King of Kucha and his consort came to court;

sentences.zh: 皆賜印綬，夫人號稱公主，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: both were bestowed seals and ribbons; the consort was styled princess, and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: both were bestowed seals and ribbons; the consort was styled princess, and rewards were very generous.

sentences.zh: ----2初作杜陵。

translations.literal: ----2 For the first time Duling was built.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 For the first time Duling was built.

sentences.zh: 徙丞相、將軍、列侯、吏二千石、訾百萬者杜陵。

translations.literal: The chancellor, generals, ranked marquises, two-thousand-bushel officials, and those with assessments of a million were moved to Duling.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor, generals, marquises, two-thousand-bushel officials, and those with assessments of a million were moved to Duling.

sentences.zh: ----3三月，詔以鳳皇集泰山、陳留，甘露降未央宮，赦天下。

translations.literal: ----3 In the third month, an edict because phoenixes gathered at Mount Tai and Chenliu and sweet dew descended at Weiyang Palace amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the third month, an edict because phoenixes gathered at Mount Tai and Chenliu and sweet dew descended at Weiyang Palace granted amnesty to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----4有司復言悼園宜稱尊號曰皇考；

translations.literal: ----4 The responsible offices again said the Garden of Mourning should be given the honored title Imperial Father;
translations.idiomatic: ----4 The responsible offices again said the Garden of Mourning should be given the honored title Imperial Father;

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，立皇考廟。

translations.literal: in summer, the fifth month, the Imperial Father Temple was established.
translations.idiomatic: in summer, the fifth month, the Imperial Father Temple was established.

sentences.zh: ----5冬，置建章衛尉。

translations.literal: ----5 In winter, the Commandant of Guards for Jianzhang was established.
translations.idiomatic: ----5 In winter, the Commandant of Guards for Jianzhang was established.

sentences.zh: ----6趙廣漢好用世吏子孫新進年少者，專厲強壯蠭氣，見事風生，無所迴避，率多果敢之計，莫為持難，終以此敗。

translations.literal: ----6 Zhao Guanghan was fond of employing sons and grandsons of hereditary officials who were newly advanced and young; he specialized in fierce, strong, waspish spirit; when he saw an affair wind arose; he avoided nothing; he mostly used bold, decisive plans and none held difficulty—he ultimately failed because of this.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Zhao Guanghan was fond of employing young sons and grandsons of hereditary officials newly advanced in office; he specialized in fierce, aggressive spirit; when he saw an affair he acted like the wind; he avoided nothing; he mostly used bold, decisive plans and none held back—he ultimately failed because of this.

sentences.zh: 廣漢以私怨論殺男子榮畜，人上書言之，事下丞相、御史按驗。

translations.literal: Guanghan because of private resentment judged and killed the man Rong Chu; people memorialized it; the matter was sent down to the chancellor and censor to investigate and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan because of private resentment judged and killed the man Rong Chu; people memorialized it; the matter was sent down to the chancellor and censor to investigate.

sentences.zh: 廣漢疑丞相夫人殺侍婢，欲以此脅丞相，丞相按之愈急。

translations.literal: Guanghan suspected the chancellor's wife had killed a serving maid and wished thereby to coerce the chancellor; the chancellor's investigation grew all the more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan suspected the chancellor's wife had killed a serving maid and wished thereby to coerce the chancellor; the chancellor's investigation grew all the more urgent.

sentences.zh: 廣漢乃將吏卒入丞相府，召其夫人跪庭下受辭，收奴婢十餘人去。

translations.literal: Guanghan thereupon led officers and soldiers into the chancellor's headquarters, summoned his wife to kneel in the courtyard below to receive interrogation, and took away more than ten slave girls.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan thereupon led officers and soldiers into the chancellor's headquarters, summoned his wife to kneel in the courtyard to be interrogated, and took away more than ten slave girls.

sentences.zh: 丞相上書自陳，事下廷尉治，實丞相自以過譴笞傅婢，出至外第乃死，不如廣漢言。

translations.literal: The chancellor memorialized in self-explanation; the matter was sent down to the Director of Justice to try; in fact the chancellor himself because of fault had reproached and flogged the attendant maid, and she died only after going out to the outer residence—not as Guanghan said.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor memorialized in self-explanation; the matter was sent down to the Director of Justice; in fact the chancellor himself because of fault had reproached and flogged the attendant maid, and she died only after going out to the outer residence—not as Guanghan said.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，下廣漢廷尉獄。

translations.literal: The emperor detested it and sent Guanghan down to the Director of Justice's prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor detested it and sent Guanghan to the Director of Justice's prison.

sentences.zh: 吏民守闕號泣者數萬人，或言：「臣生無益縣官，願代趙京兆死，使牧養小民！

translations.literal: Officials and people who guarded the gate and wept and wailed numbered tens of thousands; some said: "Your subject's life has been of no use to the district officials—I wish to die in place of Zhao, Governor of Jingzhao, and let him nurture the little people!
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people who guarded the gate and wept numbered tens of thousands; some said, "Your subject's life has been of no use to the government—I wish to die in place of Zhao, Governor of Jingzhao, and let him nurture the people!

sentences.zh: 」廣漢竟坐要斬。

translations.literal: " Guanghan in the end was punished with decapitation at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: " Guanghan in the end was executed by decapitation at the waist.

sentences.zh: 廣漢為京兆尹，廉明，威制豪強，小民得職，百姓追思歌之。

translations.literal: Guanghan as Governor of Jingzhao was incorrupt and clear, awed and restrained the powerful, and the little people obtained their posts; the people afterward remembered and sang of him.
translations.idiomatic: Guanghan as Governor of Jingzhao was incorrupt and clear, awed and restrained the powerful, and the common people obtained their due; the people afterward remembered and sang of him.

sentences.zh: ----7是歲，少府宋疇坐議「鳳皇下彭城，未至京師，不足美」，貶為泗水太傅。

translations.literal: ----7 That year, Song Chuo, Director of the Privy Purse, was punished for discussing that "the phoenix descended at Pengcheng and did not reach the capital—it is not enough to praise" and was demoted to Grand Tutor of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: ----7 That year, Song Chuo, Director of the Privy Purse, was punished for discussing that "the phoenix descended at Pengcheng and did not reach the capital—it is not enough to praise" and was demoted to Grand Tutor of Sishui.

sentences.zh: ----8上遷博士、諫大夫通政事者補郡國守相，以蕭望之為平原太守。

translations.literal: ----8 The emperor moved erudites and remonstrance grandees who understood government affairs to fill commandery and state governorships and chancellorships; Xiao Wangzhi was made Governor of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: ----8 The emperor moved erudites and remonstrance grandees who understood government affairs to fill governorships and chancellorships; Xiao Wangzhi was made Governor of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 望之上疏曰：「陛下哀愍百姓，恐德之不究，悉出諫官以補郡吏。

translations.literal: Wangzhi submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty pities the hundred surnames and fears your virtue does not reach completion, and has sent out all remonstrance officials to fill commandery posts.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi submitted a memorial, "Your Majesty pities the people and fears your virtue does not reach completion, and has sent out all remonstrance officials to fill commandery posts.

sentences.zh: 朝無爭臣，則不知過，所謂憂其末而忘其本者也。

translations.literal: With no disputing ministers at court, one will not know one's faults—what is called worrying the branch and forgetting the root.
translations.idiomatic: With no disputing ministers at court, one will not know one's faults—what is called worrying the branch and forgetting the root.

sentences.zh: 」上乃徵望之入守少府。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon summoned Wangzhi in to serve as Director of the Privy Purse.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon summoned Wangzhi in to serve as Director of the Privy Purse.

sentences.zh: ----9東海太守河東尹翁歸，以治郡高第入為右扶風。

translations.literal: ----9 Yin Wengui of Hedong, Governor of Donghai, entered as Governor of Right Fufeng for governing his commandery with top grade.
translations.idiomatic: ----9 Yin Wengui of Hedong, Governor of Donghai, entered as Governor of Right Fufeng for governing his commandery with top grade.

sentences.zh: 翁歸為人，公廉明察，郡中吏民賢、不肖及奸邪罪名盡知之。

translations.literal: Wengui as a man was fair, incorrupt, and clear-sighted; throughout the commandery he thoroughly knew which officials and people were worthy or unworthy and the names of wicked offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui was fair, incorrupt, and clear-sighted; throughout the commandery he thoroughly knew which officials and people were worthy or unworthy and the names of wicked offenses.

sentences.zh: 縣縣各有記籍，自聽其政；

translations.literal: Each county had its own registry; he himself heard their government;
translations.idiomatic: Each county had its own registry; he himself heard their government;

sentences.zh: 有急名則少緩之。

translations.literal: if there was an urgent name he would slightly ease it.
translations.idiomatic: if there was an urgent name he would slightly ease it.

sentences.zh: 吏民小解，輒披籍。

translations.literal: When officials and people slightly relaxed, he immediately opened the registry.
translations.idiomatic: When officials and people slightly relaxed, he immediately opened the registry.

sentences.zh: 取人必於秋冬課吏大會中及出行縣，不以無事時。

translations.literal: Taking people he always did at the great autumn-winter review of officials or when going out to the counties—not in times of no business.
translations.idiomatic: Taking people he always did at the great autumn-winter review of officials or when going out to the counties—not in times of no business.

sentences.zh: 其有所取也，以一警百。

translations.literal: When he took someone, he warned a hundred with one.
translations.idiomatic: When he took someone, he warned a hundred with one.

sentences.zh: 吏民皆服，恐懼，改行自新。

translations.literal: Officials and people all submitted, feared, and reformed their conduct and renewed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and people all submitted, feared, and reformed their conduct and renewed themselves.

sentences.zh: 其為扶風，選用廉平疾奸吏以為右職，接待以禮，好惡與同之；

translations.literal: When he was in Fufeng, he selected and employed incorrupt, fair, and swift-against-wicked officials for the right offices, received them with rites, and shared likes and dislikes with them;
translations.idiomatic: When he was in Fufeng, he selected and employed incorrupt, fair, and swift-against-wicked officials for the right offices, received them with rites, and shared likes and dislikes with them;

sentences.zh: 其負翁歸，罰亦必行。

translations.literal: those who failed Wengui—punishment also was surely carried out.
translations.idiomatic: those who failed Wengui—punishment was also surely carried out.

sentences.zh: 然溫良謙退，不以行能驕人，故尤得名譽於朝廷。

translations.literal: Yet he was gentle, good, humble, and yielding, and did not with conduct and ability look down on others—therefore he especially gained reputation at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was gentle, good, humble, and yielding, and did not with conduct and ability look down on others—therefore he especially gained reputation at court.

sentences.zh: ----10初，烏孫公主少子萬年有寵於莎車王。

translations.literal: ----10 At the beginning, the Wusun princess's younger son Wannian had favor with the King of Shache.
translations.idiomatic: ----10 At the beginning, the Wusun princess's younger son Wannian had favor with the King of Shache.

sentences.zh: 莎車王死而無子，時萬年在漢，莎車國人計，欲自托於漢，又欲得烏孫心，上書請萬年為莎車王。

translations.literal: The King of Shache died without a son; at that time Wannian was in Han; the people of Shache plotted, wishing to entrust themselves to Han and also wishing to win Wusun's heart, and memorialized requesting Wannian as King of Shache.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Shache died without a son; at that time Wannian was in Han; the people of Shache plotted, wishing to entrust themselves to Han and also wishing to win Wusun's heart, and memorialized requesting Wannian as King of Shache.

sentences.zh: 漢許之，遣使者奚充國送萬年。

translations.literal: Han approved and dispatched the envoy Xi Chongguo to escort Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Han approved and dispatched the envoy Xi Chongguo to escort Wannian.

sentences.zh: 萬年初立，暴惡，國人不說。

translations.literal: Wannian had just been installed and was violent and wicked; the people of the state were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wannian had just been installed and was violent and wicked; the people of the state were displeased.

sentences.zh: 上令群臣舉可使西域者，前將軍韓增舉上黨馮奉世以衛候使持節送大苑諸國客至伊循城。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to recommend one who could be sent to the Western Regions; former General Han Zeng recommended Feng Fengshi of Shangdang as envoy with staff of authority to escort guests of the various states of the Great Park to Yixun city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers to recommend one who could be sent to the Western Regions; former General Han Zeng recommended Feng Fengshi of Shangdang as envoy with staff of authority to escort guests of the various states of the Great Park to Yixun city.

sentences.zh: 會故莎車王弟呼屠徵與旁國共殺其王萬年及漢使者奚充國，自立為王。

translations.literal: It happened the former King of Shache's younger brother Hutuzheng together with neighboring states jointly killed its king Wannian and the Han envoy Xi Chongguo and installed himself as king.
translations.idiomatic: It happened the former King of Shache's younger brother Hutuzheng together with neighboring states jointly killed its king Wannian and the Han envoy Xi Chongguo and installed himself as king.

sentences.zh: 時匈奴又發兵攻車師城，不能下而去。

translations.literal: At that time the Xiongnu again dispatched troops to attack the city of Cheshi, could not take it, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xiongnu again dispatched troops to attack the city of Cheshi, could not take it, and departed.

sentences.zh: 莎車遣使揚言「北道諸國已屬匈奴矣」，於是攻劫南道，與歃盟畔漢，從鄯善以西皆絕不通。

translations.literal: Shache sent envoys proclaiming that "the states of the northern route already belong to the Xiongnu"; thereupon they attacked and plundered the southern route, swore blood alliance and turned from Han, and from Shanshan westward all communication was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Shache sent envoys proclaiming that "the states of the northern route already belong to the Xiongnu"; thereupon they attacked and plundered the southern route, swore blood alliance and turned from Han, and from Shanshan westward all communication was cut off.

sentences.zh: 都護鄭吉、校尉司馬憙皆在北道諸國間，奉世與其副嚴昌計，以為不亟擊之，則莎車日強，其勢難制，必危西域，遂以節諭告諸國王，因發其兵，南北道合萬五千人，進擊莎車，攻拔其城。

translations.literal: Protector-General Zheng Ji and Colonel Sima Xi were both among the states of the northern route; Fengshi with his deputy Yan Chang plotted, thinking that if they did not quickly strike, Shache would daily grow strong, its power hard to control, and the Western Regions would surely be endangered; they thereupon with the staff informed and told the various kings, and thereby raised their troops; north and south routes together fifteen thousand men advanced to strike Shache and stormed and took its city.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Zheng Ji and Colonel Sima Xi were both among the states of the northern route; Fengshi with his deputy Yan Chang plotted, thinking that if they did not quickly strike, Shache would daily grow strong, its power hard to control, and the Western Regions would surely be endangered; they thereupon with the staff informed the various kings and raised their troops; north and south routes together fifteen thousand men advanced to strike Shache and stormed and took its city.

sentences.zh: 莎車王自殺，傳其首詣長安，更立它昆弟子為莎車王。

translations.literal: The King of Shache killed himself; his head was transmitted to Chang'an; another kunmi's younger brother was established as King of Shache.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Shache killed himself; his head was sent to Chang'an; another kunmi's younger brother was established as King of Shache.

sentences.zh: 諸國悉平，威振西域，奉世乃罷兵以聞。

translations.literal: The various states were all pacified; authority shook the Western Regions; Fengshi thereupon dismissed the troops and reported.
translations.idiomatic: The various states were all pacified; authority shook the Western Regions; Fengshi thereupon dismissed the troops and reported.

sentences.zh: 帝召見韓增曰：「賀將軍所舉得其人。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned and saw Han Zeng and said: "Congratulations—what the general recommended obtained the right man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Han Zeng and said, "Congratulations—what the general recommended obtained the right man.

sentences.zh: 奉世遂西至大宛。

translations.literal: Fengshi thereupon went west as far as Great Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshi thereupon went west as far as Dayuan.

sentences.zh: 大宛聞其斬莎車王，敬之異於它使，得其名馬象龍而還。

translations.literal: Dayuan hearing he had beheaded the King of Shache honored him differently from other envoys; he obtained its famous horse Elephant Dragon and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Dayuan hearing he had beheaded the King of Shache honored him differently from other envoys; he obtained its famous horse Elephant Dragon and returned.

sentences.zh: 上甚說，議封奉世。

translations.literal: The emperor was very pleased and debated enfeoffing Fengshi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was very pleased and debated enfeoffing Fengshi.

sentences.zh: 丞相、將軍皆以為可，獨少府蕭望之以為：「奉世奉使有指，而擅制違命，發諸國兵，雖有功效，不可以為後法。

translations.literal: The chancellor and generals all thought it acceptable; only Director of the Privy Purse Xiao Wangzhi thought: "Fengshi on mission had instructions, yet on his own authority made policy and disobeyed orders, raising the various states' troops—though he had achievement, it cannot be made a later model.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor and generals all thought it acceptable; only Director of the Privy Purse Xiao Wangzhi thought, "Fengshi on mission had instructions, yet on his own authority made policy and disobeyed orders, raising the various states' troops—though he had achievement, it cannot be made a later model.

sentences.zh: 即封奉世，開後奉使者利以奉世為比，爭逐發兵，要功萬里之外，為國家生事於夷狄，漸不可長。

translations.literal: If Fengshi is enfeoffed, it opens the way for later envoys to profit and take Fengshi as a comparison, competing to dispatch troops and demand merit ten thousand li away, creating affairs for the state among the barbarian Di—this gradually cannot be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: If Fengshi is enfeoffed, it opens the way for later envoys to profit and take Fengshi as a comparison, competing to dispatch troops and demand merit ten thousand li away, creating affairs for the state among the barbarians—this gradually cannot be allowed to grow.

sentences.zh: 奉世不宜受封。

translations.literal: Fengshi is not fit to receive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshi is not fit to receive enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 」上善望之議，以奉世為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved Wangzhi's discussion and made Fengshi Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved Wangzhi's discussion and made Fengshi Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, the first month, there was an amnesty for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: ----2上欲立皇后，時館陶主母華倢伃及淮陽憲王母張倢伃、楚孝王母衛倢伃皆愛幸。

translations.literal: ----2 The emperor wished to establish an empress; at that time the Princess of Guantao's mother, Lady Hua of Handsome Fairness, and the King of Huaiyang Xian's mother, Lady Zhang of Handsome Fairness, and the King of Chu Xiao's mother, Lady Wei of Handsome Fairness, were all favored.
translations.idiomatic: ----2 The emperor wished to establish an empress; at that time the Princess of Guantao's mother, Lady Hua of Handsome Fairness, and the King of Huaiyang Xian's mother, Lady Zhang of Handsome Fairness, and the King of Chu Xiao's mother, Lady Wei of Handsome Fairness, were all favored.

sentences.zh: 上欲立張倢伃為-{后}-；

translations.literal: The emperor wished to establish Lady Zhang of Handsome Fairness as -{后}-;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to establish Lady Zhang of Handsome Fairness as -{后}-;

sentences.zh: 久之，懲艾霍氏欲害皇太子，乃更選後宮無子而謹慎者。

translations.literal: after long time, chastened by the Huo clan's wish to harm the crown prince, he thereupon again selected from the rear palace one without a son who was careful and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: after long time, chastened by the Huo clan's wish to harm the crown prince, he thereupon again selected from the rear palace one without a son who was careful and cautious.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙丑，立長陵王倢伃為皇后，令母養太子；

translations.literal: In the second month, on yichou, the Lady of Handsome Fairness of the King of Changling was established as empress and ordered to mother and nurture the crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yichou, the Lady of Handsome Fairness of the King of Changling was established as empress and ordered to mother and nurture the crown prince;

sentences.zh: 封其父奉光為邛成侯。

translations.literal: her father Fengguang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: her father Fengguang was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiongcheng.

sentences.zh: -{后}-無寵，希得進見。

translations.literal: -{后}- had no favor and rarely obtained advancement to audience.
translations.idiomatic: -{后}- had no favor and rarely obtained audience.

sentences.zh: ----3五月，詔曰：「獄者，萬民之命。

translations.literal: ----3 In the fifth month, an edict said: "Prisons are the lives of the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: ----3 In the fifth month, an edict said, "Prisons are the lives of the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 能使生者不怨，死者不恨，則可謂文吏矣。

translations.literal: If one can make the living not resent and the dead not hate, then one may be called a cultured official.
translations.idiomatic: If one can make the living not resent and the dead not hate, then one may be called a cultured official.

sentences.zh: 今則不然。

translations.literal: Now it is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is not so.

sentences.zh: 用法或持巧心，析律貳端，深淺不平，奏不如實，上亦亡由知，四方黎民將何仰哉！

translations.literal: In using law some hold crafty minds, split statutes into two ends, depth and shallowness not level, memorials not as in fact—the above also has no way to know; the four quarters' black-haired people—what will they look up to!
translations.idiomatic: In using law some hold crafty minds, split statutes into two ends, depth and shallowness not level, memorials not as in fact—the ruler also has no way to know; the people of the four quarters—what will they look up to!

sentences.zh: 二千石各察官屬，勿用此人。

translations.literal: Let each two-thousand-bushel official examine his subordinates and not employ such persons.
translations.idiomatic: Let each two-thousand-bushel official examine his subordinates and not employ such persons.

sentences.zh: 吏或擅興徭役，飾廚傳，稱過使客，越職逾法以取名譽，譬如踐薄冰以待白日，豈不殆哉！

translations.literal: Some officials on their own authority raise corvée labor, adorn kitchens and relay stations, praise excess to please travelers, overstep duties and exceed law to seek name and reputation—like treading thin ice waiting for the white day—is it not perilous!
translations.idiomatic: Some officials on their own authority raise corvée labor, adorn kitchens and relay stations, praise excess to please travelers, overstep duties and exceed law to seek reputation—like treading thin ice waiting for daylight—is it not perilous!

sentences.zh: 今天下頗被疾疫之災，朕甚愍之，其令郡國被災甚者，毋出今年租賦。

translations.literal: Now all under Heaven is greatly afflicted by plague disaster; We are deeply compassionate; let commanderies and kingdoms where the disaster struck severely not levy this year's rent and tax.
translations.idiomatic: Now all under Heaven is greatly afflicted by plague; We are deeply moved with pity—let commanderies and kingdoms where the disaster struck severely not levy this year's rent and tax.

sentences.zh: 」----4又曰：「聞古天子之名，難知而易諱也；

translations.literal: " ----4 He also said: "I have heard that ancient Son-of-Heaven names are hard to know and easy to taboo;
translations.idiomatic: " ----4 He also said, "I have heard that ancient Son-of-Heaven names are hard to know and easy to taboo;

sentences.zh: 其更諱詢。

translations.literal: let the taboo-name inquiry be revised.
translations.idiomatic: let the taboo-name inquiry be revised.

sentences.zh: 」----5匈奴大臣皆以為「車師地肥美，近匈奴，使漢得之，多田積穀，必害人國，不可不爭」，由是數遣兵擊車師田者。

translations.literal: " ----5 The Xiongnu great ministers all held that "Cheshi's land is fertile and fine, close to the Xiongnu; if the Han obtain it, farm much and store grain, they will surely harm our state—this cannot go uncontested," and thereby repeatedly sent troops to strike those farming Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: " ----5 The Xiongnu great ministers all held that "Cheshi's land is fertile and fine, close to the Xiongnu; if the Han obtain it, farm much and store grain, they will surely harm our state—this cannot go uncontested," and thereby repeatedly sent troops to strike those farming Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 鄭吉將渠犁田卒七千餘人救之，為匈奴所圍。

translations.literal: Zheng Ji led more than seven thousand field soldiers of Queli to rescue them and was surrounded by the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ji led more than seven thousand field soldiers of Queli to rescue them and was surrounded by the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 吉上言：「車師去渠犁千餘里，漢兵在渠犁者少，勢不能相救，願益田卒。

translations.literal: Ji submitted: "Cheshi is more than a thousand li from Queli; Han troops at Queli are few—the situation cannot allow mutual rescue; your subject wishes increased field soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji submitted, "Cheshi is more than a thousand li from Queli; Han troops at Queli are few—the situation cannot allow mutual rescue; your subject wishes increased field soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」上與後將軍趙充國等議，欲因匈奴衰弱，出兵擊其右地，使不得復擾西域。

translations.literal: " The emperor deliberated with Rear General Zhao Chongguo and others, wishing to exploit the Xiongnu's weakness, send troops to strike their right territory, and keep them from again disturbing the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor deliberated with Rear General Zhao Chongguo and others, wishing to exploit the Xiongnu's weakness, send troops to strike their right territory, and keep them from again disturbing the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 魏相上書諫曰：「臣聞之：救亂誅暴，謂之義兵，兵義者王；

translations.literal: Wei Xiang submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your subject has heard: rescuing disorder and punishing violence is called righteous troops—troops that are righteous make one king;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiang submitted a memorial remonstrating, "Your subject has heard: rescuing disorder and punishing violence is called righteous troops—troops that are righteous make one king;

sentences.zh: 敵加於己，不得已而起者，謂之應兵，兵應者勝；

translations.literal: when the enemy presses upon oneself and one rises because there is no alternative, it is called responsive troops—troops that respond win;
translations.idiomatic: when the enemy presses upon oneself and one rises because there is no alternative, it is called responsive troops—troops that respond win;

sentences.zh: 爭恨小故，不忍憤怒者，謂之忿兵，兵忿者敗；

translations.literal: contending over small causes and unable to bear angry resentment is called resentful troops—troops that resent lose;
translations.idiomatic: contending over small causes and unable to bear angry resentment is called resentful troops—troops that resent lose;

sentences.zh: 利人土地、貨寶者，謂之貪兵，兵貪者破；

translations.literal: coveting others' land and goods and treasures is called greedy troops—troops that are greedy are broken;
translations.idiomatic: coveting others' land and goods and treasures is called greedy troops—troops that are greedy are broken;

sentences.zh: 恃國家之大，矜民人之眾，欲見威於敵者，謂之驕兵，兵驕者滅。

translations.literal: relying on the state's greatness, taking pride in the people's multitude, and wishing to display might before the enemy is called arrogant troops—troops that are arrogant perish.
translations.idiomatic: relying on the state's greatness, taking pride in the people's multitude, and wishing to display might before the enemy is called arrogant troops—troops that are arrogant perish.

sentences.zh: 此五者，非但人事，乃天道也。

translations.literal: These five are not only human affairs—they are Heaven's Way.
translations.idiomatic: These five are not only human affairs—they are Heaven's Way.

sentences.zh: 間者匈奴嘗有善意，所得漢民，輒奉歸之，未有犯於邊境；

translations.literal: Recently the Xiongnu have at times shown good intent; Han people they obtained they promptly returned—there has been no offense against the border;
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Xiongnu have at times shown good intent; Han people they obtained they promptly returned—there has been no offense against the border;

sentences.zh: 雖爭屯田車師，不足致意中。

translations.literal: though they contend over garrison farming at Cheshi, it is insufficient to fix the mind upon.
translations.idiomatic: though they contend over garrison farming at Cheshi, it is insufficient to fix the mind upon.

sentences.zh: 今聞諸將軍欲興兵入其地，臣愚不知此兵何名者也！

translations.literal: Now your subject hears the various generals wish to raise troops and enter their territory—your subject in his folly does not know what name this army bears!
translations.idiomatic: Now your subject hears the various generals wish to raise troops and enter their territory—your subject in his folly does not know what name this army bears!

sentences.zh: 今邊郡困乏，父子共犬羊之裘，食草萊之實，常恐不能自存，難以動兵。

translations.literal: Now the border commanderies are exhausted; fathers and sons together wear dog-and-sheep pelts and eat wild plants' fruit—they constantly fear they cannot preserve themselves; it is hard to move troops.
translations.idiomatic: Now the border commanderies are exhausted; fathers and sons together wear dog-and-sheep pelts and eat wild plants' fruit—they constantly fear they cannot preserve themselves; it is hard to move troops.

sentences.zh: 『軍旅之後，必有凶年，』言民以其愁苦之氣傷陰陽之和也。

translations.literal: 'After armies and campaigns there must be a famine year'—meaning the people with their sorrowful, bitter qi harm the harmony of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: 'After armies and campaigns there must be a famine year'—meaning the people with their sorrowful, bitter qi harm the harmony of yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 出兵雖勝，猶有後憂，恐災害之變因此以生。

translations.literal: Sending troops out, though victorious, still has later worry—your subject fears disasters and changes will thereby arise.
translations.idiomatic: Sending troops out, though victorious, still has later worry—your subject fears disasters and changes will thereby arise.

sentences.zh: 今郡國守相多不實選，風俗尤薄，水旱不時。

translations.literal: Now commandery and kingdom governors and administrators are mostly not truthfully chosen; customs are especially thin; flood and drought come untimely.
translations.idiomatic: Now commandery and kingdom governors and administrators are mostly not truthfully chosen; customs are especially thin; flood and drought come untimely.

sentences.zh: 按今年計子弟殺父兄、妻殺夫者凡二百二十二人，臣愚以為此非小變也。

translations.literal: According to this year's tally, sons and younger brothers who killed fathers and elder brothers and wives who killed husbands totaled two hundred twenty-two persons—your subject in his folly holds this is no small change.
translations.idiomatic: According to this year's tally, sons and younger brothers who killed fathers and elder brothers and wives who killed husbands totaled two hundred twenty-two persons—your subject in his folly holds this is no small change.

sentences.zh: 今左右不憂此，乃欲發兵報纖介之忿於遠夷，殆孔子所謂『吾恐季孫之憂不在顓臾而在蕭牆之內也』。

translations.literal: Now those at left and right do not worry over this yet wish to send troops to repay a hair's breadth of resentment upon distant barbarians—perhaps what Confucius called 'I fear Ji Sun's worry is not in Zhuanyu but within the inner wall.'
translations.idiomatic: Now those at left and right do not worry over this yet wish to send troops to repay a hair's breadth of resentment upon distant barbarians—perhaps what Confucius called 'I fear Ji Sun's worry is not in Zhuanyu but within the inner wall.'

sentences.zh: 」上從相言，止。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed the chancellor's words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor followed the chancellor's words and stopped.

sentences.zh: 遣長羅侯常惠將張掖、酒泉騎往車師，迎鄭吉及其吏士還渠犁。

translations.literal: He sent Marquis Changluo Chang Hui to lead Zhangye and Jiuquan cavalry to Cheshi, welcome Zheng Ji and his officials and soldiers back to Queli.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Marquis Changluo Chang Hui to lead Zhangye and Jiuquan cavalry to Cheshi, welcome Zheng Ji and his officials and soldiers back to Queli.

sentences.zh: 召故車師太子軍宿在焉耆者，立以為王；

translations.literal: He summoned the former Cheshi crown prince Jun, who had lodged at Yanqi, and established him as king;
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the former Cheshi crown prince Jun, who had lodged at Yanqi, and established him as king;

sentences.zh: 盡徙車師國民令居渠犁，遂以車師故地與匈奴。

translations.literal: moved all Cheshi state people to dwell at Queli, and thereupon gave Cheshi's former territory to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: moved all Cheshi state people to dwell at Queli, and thereupon gave Cheshi's former territory to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 以鄭吉為衛司馬，使護善阜善以西南道。

translations.literal: He made Zheng Ji Guardian Major and had him protect the roads southwest from Shanfu and Shan.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zheng Ji Guardian Major and had him protect the roads southwest from Shanfu and Shan.

sentences.zh: ----6魏相好觀漢故事及便宜章奏，數條漢興已來國家便宜行事及賢臣賈誼、晁錯、董仲舒等所言，奏請施行之。

translations.literal: ----6 Wei Xiang delighted in examining Han precedents and expedient memorials; he repeatedly itemized since Han's rise the state's expedient measures and what worthy ministers Jia Yi, Chao Cuo, Dong Zhongshu, and others had said, memorializing to request their implementation.
translations.idiomatic: ----6 Wei Xiang delighted in examining Han precedents and expedient memorials; he repeatedly itemized since Han's rise the state's expedient measures and what worthy ministers Jia Yi, Chao Cuo, Dong Zhongshu, and others had said, memorializing to request their implementation.

sentences.zh: 相敕掾史按事郡國，及休告，從家還至府，輒白四方異聞。

translations.literal: The chancellor ordered clerks investigating affairs in commanderies and kingdoms that when on leave they returned from home to the office, they should report at once strange news from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor ordered clerks investigating affairs in commanderies and kingdoms that when on leave they returned from home to the office, they should report at once strange news from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 或有逆賊、風雨災變，郡不上，相輒奏言之。

translations.literal: If there were rebels or wind-and-rain disasters and changes that the commandery did not report upward, the chancellor would memorialize them.
translations.idiomatic: If there were rebels or wind-and-rain disasters and changes that the commandery did not report upward, the chancellor would memorialize them.

sentences.zh: 與御史大夫丙吉同心輔政，上皆重之。

translations.literal: With Censor-in-Chief Bing Ji he assisted government with one heart; the emperor valued them both.
translations.idiomatic: With Censor-in-Chief Bing Ji he assisted government with one heart; the emperor valued them both.

sentences.zh: 丙吉為人深厚，不伐善。

translations.literal: Bing Ji as a man was deep and thick and did not boast of his goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Bing Ji as a man was deep and thick and did not boast of his goodness.

sentences.zh: 自曾孫遭遇，吉絕口不道前恩，故朝廷莫能明其功也。

translations.literal: From the imperial great-grandson's encounter with fortune, Ji sealed his mouth and did not speak of former grace—therefore the court could not make clear his merit.
translations.idiomatic: From the imperial great-grandson's encounter with fortune, Ji sealed his mouth and did not speak of former grace—therefore the court could not make clear his merit.

sentences.zh: 會掖庭宮婢則令民夫上書，自陳嘗有阿保之功，章下掖庭令考問，則辭引使者丙吉知狀。

translations.literal: It happened that a Palace Rear Garden maid named Ze had a commoner husband submit a memorial, himself stating he once had wet-nurse merit; the document went down to the Palace Rear Garden director for examination—Ze in her testimony cited Envoy Bing Ji as knowing the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that a Palace Rear Garden maid named Ze had a commoner husband submit a memorial, himself stating he once had wet-nurse merit; the document went down to the Palace Rear Garden director for examination—Ze in her testimony cited Envoy Bing Ji as knowing the circumstances.

translations.literal: If worthy yet with much wealth, then their will is harmed;
translations.idiomatic: If worthy yet with much wealth, then their will is harmed;

sentences.zh: 且夫富者眾之怨也，吾既無以教化子孫，不欲益其過而生怨。

translations.literal: Moreover the wealthy are the multitude's resentment; I already have no means to transform and teach sons and grandsons—I do not wish to increase their faults and engender resentment.

translations.literal: Again, this gold is what the sage lord uses to favor and nourish an old minister—therefore I delight to share his gift with village and neighborhood and clan kin, to exhaust my remaining days—is that not acceptable!

translations.literal: His governance was fine as rice and salt, minute and dense—at first it seemed troublesome and trivial, yet Ba with full energy could carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was fine as rice and salt, minute and dense—at first it seemed troublesome and trivial, yet Ba with full energy could carry it out.

sentences.zh: 吏民見者，語次尋繹，問他陰伏以相參考，聰明識事，吏民不知所出，咸稱神明，豪厘不敢有所欺。

translations.literal: Officials and people who met him—in the course of conversation he traced and followed, asked other hidden matters to cross-reference; perceptive and knowing affairs—officials and people did not know whence it came; all called him divine, and not a hair's breadth dared any deception.

sentences.zh: 奸人去入它郡，盜賊日少。

translations.literal: Wicked men left and entered other commanderies; bandits daily grew fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men left and entered other commanderies; bandits daily grew fewer.

sentences.zh: 霸力行教化而後誅罰，務在成就全安長吏。

translations.literal: Ba strongly practiced transformation and teaching and afterward punishments, striving to complete and fully secure long-serving officials.
translations.idiomatic: Ba strongly practiced transformation and teaching and afterward punishments, striving to complete and fully secure long-serving officials.

sentences.zh: 許丞老，病聾，督郵白欲逐之。

translations.literal: Assistant Magistrate Xu was old, afflicted with deafness; the supervising clerk reported wishing to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Magistrate Xu was old, afflicted with deafness; the supervising clerk reported wishing to expel him.

sentences.zh: 霸曰：「許丞廉吏，雖老，尚能拜起送迎，正頗重聽何傷！

translations.literal: Ba said: "Assistant Magistrate Xu is an incorrupt official; though old, he can still bow, rise, and see off and welcome—what harm if he is rather hard of hearing!
translations.idiomatic: Ba said, "Assistant Magistrate Xu is an incorrupt official; though old, he can still bow, rise, and see off and welcome—what harm if he is rather hard of hearing!

sentences.zh: 且善助之，毋失賢者意！

translations.literal: Moreover, assist him well—do not lose the worthy man's intent!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, assist him well—do not lose the worthy man's intent!

sentences.zh: 」或問其故，霸曰：「數易長吏，送故迎新之費，及奸吏因緣，絕簿書，盜財物，公私費耗甚多，皆當出於民。

translations.literal: " Someone asked the reason; Ba said: "Frequently changing long officials—the expenses of seeing off the old and welcoming the new, and wicked clerks seizing opportunity, cutting off registers and documents, stealing goods and wealth—public and private costs and waste are very many; all must come from the people.
translations.idiomatic: " Someone asked the reason; Ba said, "Frequently changing long officials—the expenses of seeing off the old and welcoming the new, and wicked clerks seizing opportunity, cutting off registers and documents, stealing goods and wealth—public and private costs and waste are very many; all must come from the people.

sentences.zh: 所易新吏又未必賢，或不如其故，徒相益為亂。

translations.literal: The newly changed officials are again not necessarily worthy—perhaps not equal to the former; they only mutually increase disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The newly changed officials are again not necessarily worthy—perhaps not equal to the former; they only mutually increase disorder.

sentences.zh: 凡治道，去其泰甚者耳。

translations.literal: As for the Way of governance, one only removes what is too excessive.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Way of governance, one only removes what is too excessive.

sentences.zh: 」霸以外寬內明，得吏民心，戶口歲增，治為天下第一，徵守京兆尹。

translations.literal: " Ba, outwardly lenient and inwardly clear, won officials' and people's hearts; registered households increased year by year; his governance was rated first under Heaven—summoned to guard as Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: " Ba, outwardly lenient and inwardly clear, won officials' and people's hearts; registered households increased year by year; his governance was rated first under Heaven—summoned to guard as Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 頃之，坐法，連貶秩；

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, he sat in guilt of law and was repeatedly demoted in rank;
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter, he sat in guilt of law and was repeatedly demoted in rank;

sentences.zh: 有詔復歸穎川為太守，以八百石居。

translations.literal: an edict returned him to Yingchuan as governor, dwelling at eight hundred dan.
translations.idiomatic: an edict returned him to Yingchuan as governor, dwelling at eight hundred dan.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，詔：「年八十以上，非誣告、殺傷人，他皆勿坐。

translations.literal: 1 Spring, first month—an edict: "For those eighty years and above, except false accusation and killing or wounding people, for all else do not sit in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: 1 Spring, first month—an edict: "For those eighty years and above, except false accusation and killing or wounding people, for all else do not sit in judgment.

sentences.zh: 」----2右扶風尹翁歸卒，家無餘財。

translations.literal: " ----2 Yin Wengui, Governor of Right Fufeng, died; his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: " ----2 Yin Wengui, Governor of Right Fufeng, died; his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，詔曰：「翁歸廉平鄉正，治民異等。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month—an edict said: "Wengui was incorrupt, level, and village-upright; governing the people was of a different grade.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, eighth month—an edict said, "Wengui was incorrupt, level, and village-upright; governing the people was of a different grade.

sentences.zh: 其賜翁歸子黃金百斤，以奉祭祀。

translations.literal: Let his son be granted one hundred jin of gold to support sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: Let his son be granted one hundred jin of gold to support sacrificial rites.

sentences.zh: 」----3上令有司求高祖功臣子孫失侯者，得槐裡公乘周廣漢等百三十六人，皆賜黃金二十斤，復其家，令奉祭祀，世世勿絕。

translations.literal: " ----3 The emperor ordered the relevant offices to seek descendants of Gaozu's meritorious ministers who had lost their marquisates; they obtained Zhou Guanghan of Huaili, rank Gongcheng, and one hundred thirty-six persons—all were granted twenty jin of gold, restored their households, and ordered to maintain sacrificial rites, generation after generation never to cease.
translations.idiomatic: " ----3 The emperor ordered the relevant offices to seek descendants of Gaozu's meritorious ministers who had lost their marquisates; they obtained Zhou Guanghan of Huaili, rank Gongcheng, and one hundred thirty-six persons—all were granted twenty jin of gold, restored their households, and ordered to maintain sacrificial rites, generation after generation never to cease.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚奏狀，章下丞相、御史案驗。

translations.literal: Grand Herald memorialized the circumstances; the document went down to Chancellor and Censor for investigation and verification.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Herald memorialized the circumstances; the document went down to Chancellor and Censor for investigation and verification.

sentences.zh: 案事丞相史乃與玄成書曰：「古之辭讓，必有文義可觀，故能垂榮於後。

translations.literal: The investigating Chancellor's clerk then wrote Xuancheng a letter saying: "Ancient declinations and yieldings must have literary meaning worth viewing—therefore they could hang glory upon later generations.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating Chancellor's clerk then wrote Xuancheng a letter saying, "Ancient declinations and yieldings must have literary meaning worth viewing—therefore they could hang glory upon later generations.

sentences.zh: 今子獨壞容貌，蒙恥辱為狂癡，光曜晻而不宣，微哉子之所托名也！

translations.literal: Now my lord alone ruins his countenance, bears disgrace as mad and foolish—brilliance dim and not displayed; how slight is the name my lord trusts to!
translations.idiomatic: Now my lord alone ruins his countenance, bears disgrace as mad and foolish—brilliance dim and not displayed; how slight is the name my lord trusts to!

translations.literal: Your servant is by nature foolish and crude, in excess serving as the chancellor's agent—your servant wishes to hear a little of the wind and sound;

translations.literal: " Xuancheng's friend Gentleman-in-Attendance Zhang also submitted a memorial saying: "The sage king esteems taking ritual yielding as the state—it is fitting to favor and nourish Xuancheng, not to bend his will, so that he may secure himself beneath a plain gate.

translations.literal: The emperor esteemed his integrity and made Xuancheng Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor esteemed his integrity and made Xuancheng Governor of Henan.

translations.idiomatic: ----6 When the King of Cheshi Wugui fled to the Wusun, the Wusun detained him and did not send him away.

translations.idiomatic: The Han sent envoys to reproach the Wusun; the Wusun sent Wugui to the palace gate.

translations.idiomatic: He did not let them dwell in the Huangzhong lands.

translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Household Minister Yiqu Anguo was sent to tour the various Qiang;

translations.literal: the Xianling chieftain said: "We wish from time to time to cross north of the Huang River, following where the people do not farm to pasture livestock.
translations.idiomatic: the Xianling chieftain said, "We wish from time to time to cross north of the Huang River, following where the people do not farm to pasture livestock.

translations.literal: Rear General Zhao Chongguo impeached Anguo for disrespect on his mission.
translations.idiomatic: Rear General Zhao Chongguo impeached Anguo for disrespect on his mission.

sentences.zh: 是後羌人旁緣前言，抵冒度湟水，郡縣不能禁。

translations.literal: After this the Qiang people, edging along the former words, pressed and crossed the Huang River; commanderies and counties could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: After this the Qiang people, edging along the former words, pressed and crossed the Huang River; commanderies and counties could not forbid it.

translations.literal: Before long the Xianling and more than two hundred chieftains of various Qiang tribes dissolved enmity, exchanged hostages, and swore alliance curses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xianling and more than two hundred chieftains of various Qiang tribes dissolved enmity, exchanged hostages, and swore alliance curses.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以問趙充國，對曰：「羌人所以易制者，以其種自有豪，數相攻擊，勢不壹也。

translations.literal: The emperor heard it and questioned Zhao Chongguo; he replied: "The reason the Qiang are easy to control is that among their tribes each has its own chieftains—they repeatedly attack one another and their power is not one.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard it and questioned Zhao Chongguo; he replied, "The reason the Qiang are easy to control is that among their tribes each has its own chieftains—they repeatedly attack one another and their power is not one.

sentences.zh: 往三十餘歲西羌反時，亦先解仇合約攻令居，與漢相距，五六年乃定。

translations.literal: More than thirty years ago when the Western Qiang rebelled, they also first dissolved enmity and joined in covenant to attack Lingju, faced off with the Han, and only after five or six years was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty years ago when the Western Qiang rebelled, they also first dissolved enmity and joined in covenant to attack Lingju, faced off with the Han, and only after five or six years was it settled.

translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu repeatedly enticed the Qiang, wishing to join with them to strike Zhangye and Jiuquan territory and have the Qiang dwell there.

translations.literal: Recently the Xiongnu have been distressed in the west—your subject suspects they again sent envoys into the Qiang lands to join with them.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Xiongnu have been distressed in the west—your subject suspects they again sent envoys into the Qiang lands to join with them.

translations.literal: Your subject fears the Qiang change will not stop here but will again link with other tribes—it is fitting, while it has not yet happened, to prepare against it.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject fears the Qiang change will not stop here but will again link with other tribes—it is fitting, while it has not yet happened, to prepare against it.

translations.literal: " More than a month later, Qiang Marquis Langhe indeed sent envoys to the Xiongnu to borrow troops, wishing to strike Shanshan and Dunhuang and cut off the Han road.
translations.idiomatic: " More than a month later, Qiang Marquis Langhe indeed sent envoys to the Xiongnu to borrow troops, wishing to strike Shanshan and Dunhuang and cut off the Han road.

translations.literal: When autumn comes and horses are fat, the change will surely arise.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn comes and horses are fat, the change will surely arise.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使者行邊兵，豫為備敕，視諸羌毋令解仇，以發覺其謀。

translations.literal: It is fitting to send envoys to tour border troops, prepare instructions in advance, watch the various Qiang and not let them dissolve enmity, so as to discover their plot.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to send envoys to tour border troops, prepare instructions in advance, watch the various Qiang and not let them dissolve enmity, so as to discover their plot.

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Two Offices again reported white, sending Yiqu Anguo to tour and inspect the various Qiang, distinguishing good from bad.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Two Offices again reported white, sending Yiqu Anguo to tour and inspect the various Qiang, distinguishing good from bad.
